<!-- dfn-1: body_md -->
The $F$-signature of a big Cartier divisor $L$ on a normal projective variety $X$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ is defined to be the limit:
    \[s_X(L):= \lim_{e\xrightarrow{\ \ }\infty} \frac{1}{p^{e{(\dim X+1)}}}\sum_{m=0}^\infty\dim_k\frac{H^0(X, \mathcal O_X (mL))}{I_e(mL)},\]
    where the Frobenius-splitting subspaces $I_e (mL)$ are defined as 
    \[I_e(mL):= \{f\in H^0(X,\mathcal O_X (mL))\mid \varphi(F^e_*f) = 0 \text{ for all } \varphi \in  \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*( \mathcal O_X(mL)),\mathcal O_X)) \}.\]
<!-- end dfn-1 -->
<!-- theorema--1: body_md -->
Let $X$ be a normal projective variety over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic and $L$ be a big Cartier divisor on $X$. Then,
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textnormal{(\autoref{MainthmA})} The limit defining $s_X(L)$ exists.
\item \textnormal{(\autoref{Pn:TransformationRuleFsig})}  We have a transformation rule $s_X(L^n)= \frac{1}{n}s_X(L)$ for any $n \geq 1$.
\item \textnormal{(\autoref{thm:FsigLocallyLipschitz})} The assignment $L \mapsto \mathscr{s}_X (L)$ extends to a well-defined, locally Lipschitz continuous function on the (real) big cone of $X$.

                                                             
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorema--1 -->
<!-- theoremb--1: body_md -->
Let $X$ be a normal projective variety over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. Then, $X$ is globally $F$-regular (\autoref{dfn:globalFregularity}) if and only if the $F$-signature $s_X (L)$ with respect to some (equivalently, any) big Cartier divisor $L$ is positive.
<!-- end theoremb--1 -->
<!-- theoremc--1: body_md -->
\label{thm:theoremC}
Let $X$ be a normal projective variety over $k$. Then, \begin{enumerate}

\item\textnormal{(\autoref{Prop:Fsigandalphacomparison})} Let $L$ be a big Cartier divisor on $X$. We have the following comparison between the $F$-signature, volume function and the $\alpha_{F}$-invariant:\[ \mathscr{s}_X(L) \geq \frac{\mathrm{vol}(L) \, \alpha_{F}(X, L)^{d+1}}{(d+1)!}.\]
\item\textnormal{(\autoref{thm:positivityforbig})} Suppose further that $X$ is globally $F$-regular. Then, for any big $\mathbb{R}$-divisor $L$, the $F$-signature $s_X(L)$ is positive. Moreover, for any compact subset $\kappa$ that is contained in the big cone, there exists a constant $C>0$ (depending on $\kappa$) such that $\mathscr{s}_X(L) \geq C \mathrm{vol}(L)$ for all $L  \in \kappa$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theoremc--1 -->
<!-- theoremd--1: body_md -->
\label{thm:theoremD}
   Let $X$ be a globally $F$-regular projective variety and $L$ be a big and semi-ample divisor over $X$. Suppose $\pi: X \xrightarrow{\ \ } Y$ is the birational contraction defined by $|mL|$ for some $ m \gg 0$ sufficiently divisible and $L_0$ denote the ample divisor on $Y$ such that $\pi ^* L_0 \sim L$. Then, we have
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Suppose $K_Y $ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier and $K_{Y|X} = K_Y - \pi^* K_X \leq 0$. Then,  $\mathscr{s}_X (L) = \mathscr{s}_Y (L_0) $.

        \item Suppose $K_Y $ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier and we have $K_{Y|X} = E \geq 0$ for some effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $E$. Then, we have a natural graded sequence of ideal sheaves over $Y$ defined by
        \[ \mathfrak{a}_m := \pi_* \mathcal O_X (\lceil -mE \rceil ).  \]
        Moreover, we have the following transformation rule for the $F$-signature:
        \[ \mathscr{s}_X (L) = \mathscr{s}_Y (\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}, L_0). \]
        
        \item For any effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $\Delta_X $ such that $(X, \Delta_X)$ is globally $F$-regular and $-K_X - \Delta_X  \sim _\mathbb{Q} L$, we have:
        \begin{itemize}
            \item setting $\Delta_Y = \pi_* \Delta_X $, the pair $(Y, \Delta_Y)$ is globally $F$-regular.

            \item the divisor $- K_Y - \Delta_Y$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier and $ - K_Y - \Delta_Y \sim _\mathbb{Q} L_0 $.

            \item We have 
            \[ \mathscr{s}_X (\Delta_X, L) = \mathscr{s}_Y (\Delta_Y, L_0).\]
        \end{itemize}
        
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theoremd--1 -->
<!-- theoreme--1: body_md -->
Let $X$ be a projective variety of globally $F$-regular type over $\mathbb{C}$. Suppose we have an ample divisor $L$ and a constant $C:= C(L)$ such that for all $p \gg 0$, we have the lower bound $ \mathscr{s} (X_s, L_s) \geq C $ for all $p \gg 0$. Then, for any ample divisor $L'$ on $X$, after possibly enlarging $A$, there exists a constant $C' := C' (L')$ such that $\mathscr{s} (X_s, L'_s) \geq C'$ for all closed points $s \in \operatorname{{Spec}} (A)$ of characteristic $p$ and all $p \gg 0$.
<!-- end theoreme--1 -->
<!-- dfn-2: body_md -->
\cite{LazarsfeldPositivity1}
The \emph{ample cone} $\mathrm{Amp}(X)\subseteq N^1(X)_\mathbb{R}$ is the open convex cone of all ample $\mathbb{R}$-divisor classes. The \emph{Nef cone} $\mathrm{Nef}(X)$ is the closure of the ample cone consisting of numerically effective $\mathbb{R}$-divisor classes. We denote the \emph{cone of effective $\mathbb{R}$-divisors} by $\mathrm{Eff}(X)$ and its closure $\overline{\mathrm{Eff}}(X)$ is called the \emph{pseudo-effective cone}.
<!-- end dfn-2 -->
<!-- dfn-3: body_md -->
A divisor $D$ is $\emph{big}$ if $D$ is in the interior of the pseudo-effective cone.
<!-- end dfn-3 -->
<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:sumvol}
  Let $X$ be a $d$-dimensional normal projective variety $L$ be an invertible sheaf on $X$. Let $P(N)$ denote the function $\sum _{m = 0 } ^N  \dim_k H^0 (X, L^m)$. Then we have
  \[ \lim_{N \xrightarrow{\ \ } \infty} \frac{P(N)}{N^{d+1}/(d+1)!} = \mathrm{vol}(L).  \]
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Fix an $\varepsilon >0$. Then, by the definition of the volume function, there exists a constant $M > 0$ (depending on $\varepsilon$) such that for any $m\geq M$,
    \[\left(\mathrm{vol}(L)-  \frac{\varepsilon}{2}\right) \frac{m^d}{d!}  < \dim_k H^0 (X, L^m) < \left(\mathrm{vol}(L)+ \frac{\varepsilon}{2}\right) \frac{m^d}{d!} .\]
    Now, we take $N_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ with $M< N_0$ a sufficiently large number such that $P(M) \leq \frac{\varepsilon}{2} N_0^{d+1} /(d+1)!$. Now, for any $N\geq  N_0$, \[\begin{split} P(N)&=P(M) + \sum_{i=M+1}^N \dim_k H^0(X,L^i) \\ & < \frac{\epsilon N^{d+1}}{2(d+1)!} + \sum_{i=M+1}^N \left(\mathrm{vol}(L) +\frac{\epsilon}{2}\right)\frac{i^d}{d!} \\ &< \frac{\epsilon N^{d+1}}{2(d+1)!} + \left(\mathrm{vol}(L) +\frac{\epsilon}{2}\right) \frac{N^{d+1}}{(d+1)!} +O(N^d)\\ &= (\mathrm{vol} (L) + \epsilon) \frac{N^{d+1}}{(d+1)!}+O(N^d).\end{split}\]
    With a similar argument as above, one obtains a lower bound as follows: \[P(N)>(\mathrm{vol}(L) -\epsilon) \frac{N^{d+1}}{(d+1)!}+O(N^d).\] Therefore, for all $N \gg 0$, we have
    \[ (\mathrm{vol}(L) - \varepsilon) \frac{N^{d+1}}{(d+1)!} +O(N^d) < P (N) <  (\mathrm{vol}(L) + \varepsilon) \frac{N^{d+1}}{(d+1)!}+O(N^d).  \]
    This implies that we have
    \[ \mathrm{vol}(L) - \varepsilon \leq \liminf_{N \xrightarrow{\ \ } \infty} \frac{P(N)}{N^{d+1}/(d+1)!} \leq \limsup_{N \xrightarrow{\ \ } \infty} \frac{P(N)}{N^{d+1}/(d+1)!} \leq \mathrm{vol}(L) + \varepsilon.    \]
    Since this is true for arbitrary $\varepsilon >0$, we see that the limit $\lim_{N \xrightarrow{\ \ } \infty} \frac{P(N)}{N^{d+1}/(d+1)!} $ exists and is equal to $\mathrm{vol}(L)$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- dfn-4: body_md -->
\label{sectionringdfn}
		Let $X$ be a projective variety over $k$, $\mathcal{L}$ an ample invertible sheaf on $X$ and $\mathcal{F}$ a coherent sheaf on $X$. Then the $\mathbb{N}$-graded ring $S$ defined by
		$$ S =	S(X, \mathcal{L}) :=  \bigoplus _{n \geq 0} H^{0}(X, \mathcal{L}^{n})	$$
		is called the \emph{section ring} of $X$ with respect to $\mathcal{L}$. The affine scheme $\operatorname{{Spec}}(S)$ is called the \emph{cone over $X$} with respect to $\mathcal{L}$. The \emph{section module} of $\mathcal{F}$ with respect to $\mathcal{L}$ is a $\mbox{$\mathbb{Z}$}$-graded $S$-module $M$ defined by
		$$M = M(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{L}) := \bigoplus _{n \in \mbox{$\mathbb{Z}$}} H^{0}(X, \mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}^{n}) 	.$$
		Similarly, the sheaf corresponding to $M$ on $\operatorname{{Spec}}(S)$ is called the \emph{cone over $\mathcal{F}$} with respect to $\mathcal{L}$.
<!-- end dfn-4 -->
<!-- lem-2: body_md -->
\label{lem.SectionRingVSCoherentSheaf} Let $X$ be a projective variety over $k$ and $\mathcal{L}$ an ample invertible sheaf over $X$. 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The section ring $S$ of $X$ with respect to $\mathcal{L}$ is always finitely generated over $k$ and hence, is Noetherian.  If $X$ is normal, then the section ring is also characterized as the unique normal $\mathbb{N}$-graded ring $S$ such that $\operatorname{{Proj}}(S)$ is isomorphic to $X$ and the corresponding $\mathcal O_X(1)$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal{L}$.
    \item The section module of any coherent sheaf over $X$ with respect to $\mathcal{L}$ is finitely generated over $S$. It is also characterized as the unique saturated (with respect to the homogeneous maximal ideal) $S$-module $M$ such that the associated coherent sheaf $\tilde{M}$ on $X$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal{F}$. 
    \item For two coherent sheaves $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$, we have a natural isomorphism:
    $$ \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G})  \cong \operatorname{Hom}^{\text{gr}}_{S}(M(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{L}), M(\mathcal{G}, \mathcal{L}))     $$
    where $\operatorname{Hom} ^{\text{gr}} _S(\, , \, )$ denotes the set of grading preserving $S$-module maps between two graded $S$-modules. 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
See \cite[\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BXF}{Tag 0BXF}]{stacks-project}.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- dfn-5: body_md -->
\label{dfn:globalFregularity}
Let $X$ be a normal variety over an algebraically closed field $k$ of positive characteristic. $X$ is globally $F$-regular if for any effective Weil divisor $D$ on $X$, there exists some integer $e>0$ such that the natural map $\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\ \ } F^e_*\mathcal O_X(D)$ splits as a map of $\mathcal O_X$-modules.
<!-- end dfn-5 -->
<!-- dfn-6: body_md -->
\label{Iedfn}
Let $X$ be normal projective variety over $k$ and $D$ denote any Weil divisor on $X$. Then, for any integer $e \geq 1$, we define a $k$-vector subspace $I_e(D)$ of $H^0 (D):= H^0 (X, \mathcal O_X(D)) $ as \[I_e(D):= \{f\in H^0(D)\mid \varphi(F^e_*f) = 0 \text{ for all } \varphi \in  \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*( \mathcal O_X(D)),\mathcal O_X)) \}.\]
<!-- end dfn-6 -->
<!-- lem-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:Ieeffective}
    Let $X$ be a normal, projective variety over $k$ and $D$ and $E$ be effective Weil divisors on $X$. Note that the effective divisor $E$ defines an inclusion $H^0 (X, \mathcal O_X(D)) \subset H^0 (X, \mathcal O_X(D+E))$. Then, for any $e \geq 1$, we have
    \[ I_e (D) \subset I_e (D+E). \]
<!-- end lem-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
See \cite[Lemma 4.12]{LeePandeFsigAmpCone}.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\cite[Theorem 4.9]{LeePandeFsigAmpCone}\label{Thm:DegenSpaceEqualsWholeSpace}
Let $X$ be a normal projective variety over $k$ with $\dim(X)>0$. Fix a norm $\|\|$ on the N\'eron-Severi space $N^1_\mathbb{R}(X)$. Let $L$ be an effective Cartier divisor such that $\|L\|\neq 0$. Then, there exists a constant $C$ depending only on $X$ and the norm such that for any effective Cartier $H$ on $X$, we have: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $I_e(mL) = H^0(mL)$ for all $e\geq 1$ and $m> Cp^e/\|L\|$
\item For all $n>2\|H\|/\|L\|$, \[I_e(m(nL+H))=H^0(m(nL+H)) \text{ for all $e\geq 1$ and $m>\frac{Cp^e}{n\|L\|}$}.\] 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- dfn-7: body_md -->
(\cite{VonKorffthesis},\cite{LeePandeFsigAmpCone})
    Let $X$ be a globally $F$-regular projective variety over $k$. Suppose that $d=\dim(X)>0$. Let $L$ be an ample $\mathbb{R}$-divisor on $X$. Then, the $F$-signature function $\mathscr{s}_X(L)$ is defined as \[\mathscr{s}_X(L) = \lim_{e\xrightarrow{\ \ }\infty}\frac{1}{p^{e(d+1)}}\sum_{m=0}^\infty\dim_k \frac{H^0(mL)}{I_e(mL)}.\]
<!-- end dfn-7 -->
<!-- dfn-8: body_md -->
\label{dfn:Fsigbig} \label{Dfn.FsigBigDivisors}
    The $F$-signature of a $d$-dimensional normal projective variety $X$ with respect to a big Cartier divisor $L$ on $X$ is defined to be
    \begin{equation}\label{eqn:FsigFormula}
    \mathscr{s} _X (L) : = \lim_{e\xrightarrow{\ \ }\infty}\frac{1}{p^{e(d+1)}}\sum_{m=0}^\infty\dim_k \frac{H^0(mL)}{I_e(mL)}\end{equation}
<!-- end dfn-8 -->
<!-- thm-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:Fsigbigexists} \label{MainthmA}
    The limit \autoref{eqn:FsigFormula} defining the $F$-signature of a big divisor exists.
<!-- end thm-2 -->
<!-- rem-1: body_md -->
The sum in the formula \autoref{eqn:FsigFormula} is finite for each $e \geq 1$. Indeed, by \autoref{Thm:DegenSpaceEqualsWholeSpace}, there exists a constant $C$ such that $H^0(mL) = I_e(mL)$ for all $m>Cp^e/\|L\|$.
<!-- end rem-1 -->
<!-- rem-2: body_md -->
If $L$ is ample, then \autoref{dfn:Fsigbig} coincides with the $F$-signature of the section ring $S (X, L)$ over $X$ \cite[Theorem 3.3]{LeePandeFsigAmpCone}.
<!-- end rem-2 -->
<!-- lem-4: body_md -->
\label{Lem.LimitExists}\cite[Lemma 3.5.(ii)]{PolstraTuckerCombinedApproach} Let $p$ be a prime number and $d$ be a natural number. Let $a_e$ be a sequence of positive real numbers such that $a_e/p^{e(d+1)}$ is bounded. Suppose that there exists a positive number $C$ such that \begin{equation}\label{Eqn.Existence}\frac{a_e}{p^{e(d+1)}}\leq \frac{a_{e+1}}{p^{(e+1)(d+1)}}+\frac{C}{p^e} \text{ for all }e \in \mathbb{N}\end{equation} Then the limit $a= \lim_{e\xrightarrow{\ \ }\infty} \frac{a_e}{p^{e(d+1)}}$ exists.
<!-- end lem-4 -->
<!-- lem-5: body_md -->
\label{Lem.LimitComparison} Let $L$ be a big divisor on $X$ and fix a constant $C_1 >0$ as in \autoref{Thm:DegenSpaceEqualsWholeSpace}. Suppose there exists a Cartier divisor $D$ such that for each $0 \leq j \leq p-1$, we have an inclusion
\[ \iota_{j}: F_*\mathcal O_X(jL) \hookrightarrow  \mathcal O_X (D)^{\oplus p^{d}}.\]
Then, there exists a constant $C_2>0$ such that for all $e \geq 1$ and for all $m<C_1p^e$, we have \[p^d \dim_k \frac{H^0(D+\lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L)}{I_e(D+\lfloor\frac{m}{p}\rfloor L)} \leq \dim_k \frac{H^0(mL)}{I_{e+1}(mL)} + C_{2}p^{(e-1)(d-1)}.\]
<!-- end lem-5 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
If $m=0$, we may take $C_2=2p^d\dim_k H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(D))$. Then, \[p^d \dim_k \frac{H^0(D)}{I_e(D)} \leq \dim_k \frac{H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)}{I_{e+1}(0)} + C_{2}p^{(e-1)(d-1)} \text{ for all $e\geq 1$}.\] Hence, we assume $m\geq 1$. For each $m \geq 1$, let us write $m=p\lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor+j_m$ for some $0 \leq j_m \leq p-1$. For each $e\geq 1$, consider an inclusion given by $\iota_{j_m}: F_*\mathcal O_X(j_mL)\xrightarrow{\ \ } \mathcal O_X(D)^{\oplus p^d}$. Let $\iota_{e,m}$ denote the inclusion
\begin{equation}\label{eqn.IotaMapDefn} \iota_{e,m}: F^{e+1}_* \mathcal O_X(mL) \xrightarrow{\ \ } F^e_*\mathcal O_X\left(D+\left\lfloor\frac{m}{p} \right\rfloor L\right)^{\oplus p^{d}} \end{equation}
obtained by twisting $\iota_{j_m}$ by the invertible sheaf $\mathcal O_X(\lfloor \frac{m}{p} \rfloor L)$ and taking the $e$-th iterated Frobenius pushforward.

Now, for each $e\geq 1$ and $1\leq m <C_1p^e $, consider the following exact sequence \begin{equation}\label{Eqn.ExactSeqCokercomputation} 0 \xrightarrow{\ \ }  F^{e+1}_* \mathcal O_X(mL) \stackrel{\iota_{e,m}}{\xrightarrow{\ \ }} F^e_*\mathcal O_X\left(D+\left\lfloor\frac{m}{p} \right\rfloor L\right)^{\oplus p^{d}} \xrightarrow{\ \ } \operatorname{{coker}}(\iota_{e,m}) \xrightarrow{\ \ } 0. \end{equation}
For simplicity, set $\ell = \lfloor \frac{m}{p} \rfloor $. Then,
\[\operatorname{{coker}} \iota_{e,m} = \frac{F^e_*\mathcal O_X(D + \ell L)^{\oplus p^d}}{F^{e+1}_*\mathcal O_X((j_m+\ell p)L)} = F^e_*\left(\frac{\mathcal O_X(D)^{\oplus p^d}}{F_*\mathcal O_X(j_mL)}\otimes \mathcal O_X(\ell L) \right).\]

Let $Q_{j}$ be the cokernel of $\iota_j: F_*\mathcal O_X (jL) \xrightarrow{\ \ } \mathcal O_X(D)^{\oplus p^d}$ and $Z_j$ denote the support of $Q_j$. Since $\iota_j$ is generically an isomorphism, $\dim Z_j \leq d-1$. For each $0 \leq j \leq p-1$, choose a very ample divisor $A_j$ on $Z_j$ such that the support of $A_j - L|_{Z_j}$ is effective and avoids all the associated points of $A_j$. In other words, locally on $Z_j$, the function defining $A_j - L|_{Z_j}$ is a non-zero divisor on $Q_j$. This ensures that for each $j$ and $ \ell \geq 1$, we an injective map
\[ Q_j \otimes \mathcal O_X (\ell L) \hookrightarrow Q_j (\ell A_j). \]


Note that since $\iota_{e,m}$ is obtained by twisting $\iota _{j_m}$, the cokernel of $\iota_{j_m}$ is also supported on $Z_{j_m}$. By the asymptotic Riemann-Roch formula \cite[Example 1.2.9]{LazarsfeldPositivity1}, there exist constants $C', C_0 > 0$ such that \begin{equation}\label{Eqn.CokernelComputation}\begin{split}\dim_k H^0(\operatorname{{coker}}\iota_{e,m})&= H^0\left(Q_{j_m}\otimes \mathcal O_X(\ell L) \right) \leq H^0\left(Q_{j_m}\otimes \mathcal O_X(\ell A_{j_m}) \right) \\
& \leq   C'\ell^{d-1} +O(l^{d-2})\leq C_0 \ell ^{d-1} \leq  C_0\left(\frac{m}{p}\right)^{d-1}< C p^{(e-1)(d-1)}, \end{split}\end{equation}
where we set $C = C_0C_1^{d-1}$ and we have used that $\ell \leq m/p \leq C_1 p^{e-1}$ since $m \leq C_1 p^e$.


Now, consider a map $\Psi$ defined by the composition of \[H^0(mL) \xrightarrow{\ \ } H^0\left( D+ \left\lfloor \frac{m}{p}\right\rfloor L\right)^{\oplus p^d}\xrightarrow{\ \ } \left(\frac{H^0\left( D+ \lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L\right)}{I_e\left( D+ \lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L\right)}\right)^{\oplus p^d}.\] We have the exact sequence \[0\xrightarrow{\ \ } \ker\Psi \xrightarrow{\ \ } H^0(mL) \stackrel{\Psi}{\xrightarrow{\ \ }}\left(\frac{H^0\left( D+ \lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L\right)}{I_e\left( D+ \lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L\right)}\right)^{\oplus p^d} \xrightarrow{\ \ } \operatorname{{coker}} \Psi \xrightarrow{\ \ } 0.\] Now, we claim that $I_{e+1}(mL)\subseteq \ker\Psi$. Indeed, we have the image of $I_{e+1}(mL)$ in $H^0(D+\lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L)$ is contained in $ I_e\left( D+ \lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L\right)$. If not, there is a section $s\in I_{e+1}(mL)$ whose image is not contained in $I_e\left( D+ \lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L\right)$. Then, via \autoref{eqn.IotaMapDefn}, we have a map $F^{e+1}_*\mathcal O_X(mL) \xrightarrow{\ \ } F^e_*\mathcal O_X\left( D+ \lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L\right)^{\oplus p^d}\xrightarrow{\ \ } \mathcal O_X$ sending $s\mapsto 1$, which contradicts the fact that $s$ is a non-splitting section. 

Therefore,  we have the bounds \[\begin{split} p^d\dim_k\frac{H^0\left( D+ \lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L\right)}{I_e\left( D+ \lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L\right)}&\leq \dim_k\frac{H^0(mL)}{\ker \Psi}+\dim_k \operatorname{{coker}}\Psi \\ &\leq \dim_k\frac{H^0(mL)}{I_{e+1}(mL)}+\dim_k \operatorname{{coker}}\Psi .\end{split}\]
Now, we bound the dimension of the cokernel of $\Psi$: \begin{align*}\dim_k\operatorname{{coker}} \Psi &= \dim_k\frac{H^0\left( D+ \lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L\right)^{\oplus p^d}}{H^0(mL)+ I_e\left( D+ \lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L\right)^{\oplus p^d}} &\leq \dim_k\frac{H^0\left( D+ \lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L\right)^{\oplus p^d}}{H^0(mL)}\\
&&  \leq H^0(\operatorname{{coker}}\iota_{e,m}) \leq Cp^{(e-1)(d-1)} .\end{align*}
The last inequality holds thanks to \autoref{Eqn.CokernelComputation}. This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lem-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:injectivemap}
    Let $X$ be a normal, projective variety of dimension $d$ and $L$ be any Cartier divisor on $X$. Then, there exists a Cartier divisor $D$ such that for each $0 \leq j \leq p-1$, we have an injective map
    \begin{equation} \label{injectivemap} \iota_j: F_* (\mathcal O_X(jL)) \hookrightarrow \mathcal O_X(D) ^{\oplus p^d}.\end{equation}
    Moreover, we may assume that $D$ is effective and defines a normal subscheme of $X$.
<!-- end lem-6 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Fix an ample divisor $H$ on $X$. Since $H$ is ample, there exists an $M \gg 0$ such that for all $m \geq M$ and all $0 \leq j \leq p-1$, the sheaf
    \[ \mathscr{H}om_{\mathcal O_X}(F_* (\mathcal O_X(jL)), \mathcal O_X(mH) ) \cong F_* (\mathcal O_X((1-p)K_X - jL )) \otimes \mathcal O_X(mH)    \]
    is generated by its global sections. Here, we have used the duality isomorphism for the Frobenius as expalined in \cite[Section 4.1]{SchwedeSmithLogFanoVsGloballyFRegular}. In particular, we may assume that each of these sheaves is globally generated at the generic point of $X$. Let $\eta$ denote the generic point of $X$ and consider the following restriction map to the generic stalk:    
    \begin{equation} \label{globalgeneratedhom} \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X} (F_*(\mathcal O_X(jL)), \mathcal O_X(mH))  \xrightarrow{\ \ } \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{X, \eta}} (F_* (\mathcal O_X(jL)) _{\eta}), \mathcal O_X(mH) _{\eta} ). \end{equation}
    Since $\mathscr{H} om _{\mathcal O_{X}} \big( \,  (F_*(\mathcal O_X(jL)), \mathcal O_X(mH)) \, \big)$ is generically globally generated, this means that the image of the map in \autoref{globalgeneratedhom} generates $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{X, \eta}} (F_* (\mathcal O_X(jL))_{\eta}), \mathcal O_X(mH) _{\eta} )$ as an $\mathcal O_{X, \eta}$-module. Recall that $\mathcal O_{X, \eta}$ is just the fraction field of $X$. Since $F_* (\mathcal O_X(jL)) _{\eta})$ is a free $\mathcal O_{X , \eta}$-vector space of rank $p^{d}$, we can choose $p^{d}$ maps $\phi_{1}, \dots, \phi_{p^{d}}$ in $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X} (F_*(\mathcal O_X(jL)), \mathcal O_X(mH)) $ such that their images under the map in \autoref{globalgeneratedhom} forms a basis of $  \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{X, \eta}} (F_* (\mathcal O_X(jL)) _{\eta}), \mathcal O_X(mH) _{\eta} )$ over $\mathcal O_{X, \eta}$. Thus, defining $\iota _{j,m}$ to be the product map 
    \[  \iota _{j,m}: = \phi_{1} \times \dots \times \phi_{p^{d}} : F_*(\mathcal O_X(jL)) \rightarrow \mathcal O_X(mH) ^{\oplus p^{d}} ,\]
    we see that $\iota_{j,m}$ is generically an isomorphism by construction. Furthermore, since $F_* (\mathcal O_X(jL))$ is a torsion-free sheaf of rank $p^{d}$ over $\mathcal O_{X}$, $\iota_{j,m}$ is injective since it is generically an isomorphism. This completes that proof of the claim that maps as in \autoref{injectivemap} exist for each $m \geq M$. Now since $H$ is ample, we may pick $m \gg 0$ so that we can find an effective divisor $D$ in the linear system $|mH|$. Since $X$ is assumed to be normal, by Bertini's theorem, a general such divisor $D$ is  normal by \cite[Corollary 3.4.14]{FlennerJoins}.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- dfn-9: body_md -->
Let $\Delta$ be an effective $\mathbb{Q}$-Weil divisor on $X$. For any Weil divisor $L$ on $X$ and $e\geq 1$, define the $k$-vector subspace $I^\Delta_e(L)$ of $H^0
(X, \mathcal O_X(L))$ as follows:
\[I_e^\Delta(L) = \{ s \in H^0(L) \mid \varphi(F^e_* s) = 0 \text{ for all } \varphi \in \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(\lceil (p^e-1)\Delta \rceil +L, \mathcal O_X)\}\]
<!-- end dfn-9 -->
<!-- lem-7: body_md -->
\cite[Lemma 2.18]{PandeFrobeniusVersionTiansAlphaInvariant}\label{Lem.PandeDuality}
Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a normal projective pair, and let $D$ be any Weil divisor on $X$. Then, denoting $D_1= (1-p^e)K_X-\lceil (p^e-1)\Delta\rceil-D$ and $D_2 = (1-p^e)K_X-\lceil (p^e-1)\Delta\rceil$ for any $e\geq 1$, we have a non-degenerate pairing \[\frac{H^0(D)}{I_e^{\Delta}(D)}\times \frac{H^0(D_1)}{I_e^{\Delta}(D_1)}\xrightarrow{\ \ } \frac{H^0(D_2)}{I_e^{\Delta}(D_2)}\] obtained from multiplication (and reflexifying) global sections. In particular, \[\dim_k\frac{H^0(D)}{I_e^{\Delta}(D)}=
\dim_k\frac{H^0(D_1)}{I_e^{\Delta}(D_1)}.\]
<!-- end lem-7 -->
<!-- pn-1: body_md -->
\label{Pn:twistedFsig}
Let $X$ be a normal projective variety over $k$ of positive dimension and $L$ a big divisor on $X$. Assume $H^0 (X, \mathcal O_X) = k$. Fix a Cartier divisor $D$ on $X$. Then, there exists a constant $C >0$ (depending only on $D$ and $L$) such that
$$ \left| \dim_{k}\frac{H^{0}(mL)}{I_{e}(mL)} - \dim_{k}\frac{H^{0}(mL+D)}{I_{e}(mL+D)} \right| \leq C p^{e(\dim(X) - 1)} $$
for all $m \geq 0$ and $e>0$.
<!-- end pn-1 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
The case when $m=0$ is straightforward since it is bounded by $1+\dim_kH^0(D)$ which is a constant. Hence, we may assume $m\geq 1$.  First, we consider the case when $D$ is effective. By using the natural map $\mathcal O_{X}(mL) \xrightarrow{\ \ } \mathcal O_{X}(mL+D)$, we will view $H^{0}(mL)$ as a subspace of $H^{0}(mL+D)$. Let $J_{e}(mL)$ denote the subspace $H^{0}(mL) \cap I_{e}(mL+D)$. By \cite[Lemma 4.12]{LeePandeFsigAmpCone}, we see that $I_{e}(mL) \subset J_{e}(mL)$. Furthermore, recall that we have an inclusion \begin{equation}\label{eqn.IeJeComparison}\frac{H^0 (mL)}{J_e(mL)} \hookrightarrow \frac{H^0(mL+D)}{I_e(mL+D)}\end{equation} coming from the inclusion $H^0(mL)\hookrightarrow H^0(mL+D)$. 
Now, the cokernel of \autoref{eqn.IeJeComparison} is $H^0(mL+D)/(H^0(mL)+I_e(mL+D))$, so this induces
\begin{equation} \label{eqn.DimensionComparison}\dim_{k}\frac{H^{0}(mL+D)}{I_{e}(mL+D)} = \dim_{k}\frac{H^{0}(mL)}{J_{e}(mL)} + \dim_{k}\frac{H^{0}(mL+D)}{H^0 (mL) + I_{e}(mL+D)}.\end{equation}
Using \autoref{eqn.DimensionComparison} and the triangle inequality, we obtain that
\begin{equation} \label{firstestimate} 
\begin{split}
 & \left| \dim_{k}\frac{H^{0}(mL)}{I_{e}(mL)} - \dim_{k}\frac{H^{0}(mL+D)}{I_{e}(mL+D)} \right| \\ 
 = & \left|\dim_k \frac{H^0(mL)}{I_e(mL)}-\dim_k\frac{H^0(mL)}{J_e(mL)} - \dim_k\frac{H^0(mL+D)}{H^0(mL)+I_e(mL+D)}\right|
 \\ \leq &\left|\dim_k \frac{H^0(mL)}{I_e(mL)}-\dim_k\frac{H^0(mL)}{J_e(mL)} \right| + \dim_k\frac{H^0(mL+D)}{H^0(mL)+I_e(mL+D)}
\\  \leq &  \dim_{k}\frac{J_{e}(mL)}{I_{e}(mL)}+\dim_{k} \frac{H^{0}(mL+D)}{H^{0}(mL)} 
\end{split}
\end{equation}
for all $m, e>0$. Now, we bound each term in the above inequality. To compute the first term, we fix an $e>0$ and set $\Delta_e = \frac{1}{p^e -1} D$. Then, we observe that the subspace $J_e (mL)$ is exactly the same as $I_e ^{\Delta_e} (mL)$ by construction. Moreover, we also similarly have 
\begin{equation} \label{dualJe} I_e ^{\Delta_e} ((1-p^e)K_X - mL-D) = H^0 ((1-p^e)K_X - mL -D) \cap I_e ((1-p^e)K_X - mL) .\end{equation}
Thus, by \autoref{Lem.PandeDuality}, we have
\[ \dim_k \frac{H^0 (mL)}{I_e (mL)}  = \dim_k \frac{H^0 ((1-p^e)K_X - mL)}{I_e ((1-p^e)K_X - mL)} \]
and similarly,
\[ \dim_k \frac{H^0 (mL)}{J_e (mL)}  = \dim_k \frac{H^0 ((1-p^e)K_X - mL -D)}{I_e ^{\Delta_e} ((1-p^e)K_X - mL-D)} .\]
By \autoref{dualJe}, we see 
the natural map from $H^0 ((1-p^e)K_X - mL -D)$ to $ H^0 ((1-p^e)K_X - mL)$ restricts to an \emph{injective} map
\[ \frac{H^0 ((1-p^e)K_X - mL -D)}{I_e ^{\Delta_e} ((1-p^e)K_X - mL-D)} \hookrightarrow \frac{H^0 ((1-p^e)K_X - mL)}{I_e ((1-p^e)K_X - mL)} .\]
By considering the cokernel of this map, we get that
\begin{equation} \label{secondestimate}
   \dim_{k}\frac{J_{e}(mL)}{I_{e}(mL)} = \dim_{k}\frac{H^{0}(mL)}{I_{e}(mL)} - \dim_{k}\frac{H^{0}(mL)}{J_{e}(mL)} \leq  \dim_{k} \frac{H^{0}((1-p^e)K_{X} -mL)}{H^{0}((1-p^e)K_{X} -mL-D)}.
\end{equation}


Pick an $M \gg 0$ such that following conditions hold for the linear system $|ML|$: there is an effective divisor $E_2 \in |ML|$ and an effective Weil-divisor $E_3$ such that $E_2 - E_3 \sim -K_X$. We can do this by choosing $M$ such that $H^0 (X,\mathcal O_X(K_X+ ML)) \neq 0$ since $\mathcal O_X(K_X+ML)$ is generically globally generated.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               

Now, we pick a very ample divisor $H \subset X$ such that there is a divisor $E \in |H|$ that defines a normal subscheme of $X$. This can be done by Bertini's theorems for normal varieties \cite[Corollary 3.4.14]{FlennerJoins}. Moreover, we may do this in such a way that $E$ does not share components with $E_2$ or $E_3$ and there exists an effective Cartier divisor $E_1$ such that $D + E_1 \sim E$. We may also assume, by enlarging $M$ chosen if necessary, that the linear systems $|mL|$ for $m \geq M$ contain a divisor not vanishing along $E$. This is possible since $L$ is big. 
Now, using the divisor $E_1$, we get that
\[  \dim_{k} \frac{H^{0}((1-p^e)K_{X} -mL)}{H^{0}((1-p^e)K_{X} -mL-D)} \leq \dim_k  \frac{H^{0}((1-p^e)K_{X} -mL)}{H^{0}((1-p^e)K_{X} -mL-E)}.  \]
Next, since the divisor $E$ does not share  components with $E_2, E_3 $, for any $e \geq 1$, we may restrict the Weil divisor $(1-p^e) K_X - mL \sim (p^e-1)(E_2 - E_3) - mL$ to $E$ (as explained in \autoref{restrictingWeildivisors}). In conclusion, using \autoref{restrictingtonormaldivisorexactsequence}, we get
\[ \dim_{k}\frac{J_{e} (mL)}{I_{e} (mL)} \leq \dim_{k} H^{0}((p^e-1)(E_2 - E_3)|_E -mL|_E ).  \]
Furthermore, since by assumption, $mL$ also admits a section that does not share a component with $E$, we in fact have:
\begin{equation} \label{thirdestimate}
    \dim_{k} \frac{J_{e} (mL)}{I_{e} (mL)} \leq \dim_k H^0 ((p^e -1) E_2 |_E)  = \frac{\mathrm{vol}(E_2|_E)}{(d-1)!} p^{e(d-1)} + O(p^{e(d-2)})
\end{equation}
 and 
 \begin{equation} \label{fourthestimate}
     \dim_{k} \frac{H^{0}(mL+D)}{H^{0}(mL)}  \leq \frac{\mathrm{vol}(L|_D)}{(d-1)!} m^{d-1} + O(m^{d-2})
 \end{equation}
 
 Finally, by \cite[Theorem 4.9]{LeePandeFsigAmpCone}, we may pick a constant $C_{2}>0$ such that $H^{0}(mL) = I_{e}(mL)$ and $H^{0}(mL+D) = I_{e}(mL+D)$ for $m >C_{2}p^{e}$. Therefore, to prove the Proposition, it is enough to consider the case when $m \leq C_{2} p^{e}$. In this case, the Proposition now follows by putting together inequalities in \ref{firstestimate}, \ref{secondestimate}, \ref{thirdestimate} and \ref{fourthestimate}. This completes the proof of the Proposition in the case when $D$ is effective.

 
 More generally, when $D$ is not necessarily effective, since $L$ is big, we first pick a fixed number $r \gg 0$ such that $rL$ and $D+ rL$ are both effective. Then, for any $ e \geq 1$ and $m > r$, we have
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
 \left| \dim_{k}\frac{H^{0}(mL)}{I_{e} (mL)} - \dim_{k}\frac{H^{0}(mL+D)}{I_{e}(mL+D)} \right| \leq & \left| \dim_{k}\frac{H^{0}(mL)}{I_{e} (mL)} - \dim_{k}\frac{H^{0}((m-r)L)}{I_{e}  ((m-r)L)} \right| \\
 + &\left| \dim_{k}\frac{H^{0}((m-r)L)}{I_{e}  ((m-r)L)} - \dim_{k}\frac{H^{0}((m-r)L + rL+D)}{I_{e}  ((m-r)L+rL+D)} \right| .
 \end{split}   \end{equation*}
 Now, we may apply the previous case of the Proposition (since both $D+rL$ and $rL$ are effective) to each of the two terms in the above inequality. Since $r$ was independent of $e$, this completes the proof of the Proposition.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Set \[a_e = \sum_{m=0}^\infty \dim_k\frac{H^0(mL)}{I_e(mL)}.\] To show the existence of $\mathscr{s}_X(L)$, using \autoref{Lem.LimitExists}, we need to check the following: \begin{enumerate}
\item $\displaystyle\frac{a_e}{p^{e(d+1)}}$ is bounded above.
\item there is some constant $C$ such that $\displaystyle\frac{a_e}{p^{e(d+1)}}\leq \frac{a_{e+1}}{p^{(e+1)(d+1)}}+\frac{C}{p^e} \text{ for all }e \in \mathbb{N}.$
\end{enumerate}
We first prove part (a). Using \autoref{Thm:DegenSpaceEqualsWholeSpace}, we fix $C_0>0$ such that $H^0(mL) = I_e(mL)$ whenever $m> C_0p^e$. Then, \[ a_e = \sum_{m=0}^{ C_0p^e} \dim_k\frac{H^0(mL)}{I_e(mL)} \leq \sum_{m=0}^{C_0p^e}\dim_k H^0(mL) \leq \tilde{C}\mathrm{vol}(L)p^{e(d+1)} + O(p^{ed}) \]
for some $\tilde{C} >0$, where the last inequality uses \autoref{lem:sumvol}.
Dividing by $p^{e(d+1)}$, we see that $a_e/p^{e(d+1)}$ is bounded above. 

For part (b), choose a Cartier divisor $D$ and a injective map $\iota_j : F_*\mathcal O_X(jL)\xrightarrow{\ \ } \mathcal O_X(D)^{\oplus p^d}$ for each $0 \leq j \leq p -1$, as in \autoref{lem:injectivemap}.
We again fix a constant $C_0>0$ such that $H^0(mL) = I_e(mL)$ for all $m>C_0p^e$. Then \[\begin{split} p^d\dim_k \frac{H^0(\lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L)}{I_e(\lfloor \frac{m}{p} \rfloor L)} & = p^d \left(\dim_k \frac{H^0(\lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L)}{I_e(\lfloor \frac{m}{p} \rfloor L)} - \dim_k \frac{H^0(\lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L + D)}{I_e(\lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L + D)} \right) + p^d\dim_k \frac{H^0(\lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L + D)}{I_e(\lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L + D)} \\ & \leq p^d C_1p^{e(d-1)} +  p^d\dim_k \frac{H^0(\lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L + D)}{I_e(\lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L + D)} \text{  (by \autoref{Pn:twistedFsig})} \\ &\leq C_1 p^{e(d-1)+d}+\dim_k \frac{H^0(mL)}{I_{e+1}(mL)} + C_{2}p^{(e-1)(d-1)} \text{ (by \autoref{Lem.LimitComparison})}.\end{split}\] 
Dividing by $p^{(e+1)(d+1)}$ for both sides, we obtain \begin{equation}\label{eqn.Fsigexistscomputation}\frac{1}{p^{e(d+1) + 1}}\dim_k \frac{H^0(\lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L)}{I_e(\lfloor \frac{m}{p} \rfloor L)} \leq \frac{1}{p^{(e+1)(d+1)}}\dim_k \frac{H^0(mL)}{I_{e+1}(mL)} +
\frac{C_1}{p^{2e+1}} + O(\frac{1}{p^{2e + 2d +2}} ).\end{equation} 
Moreover, we pick a constant $C_3 > 0$ such that the error term $\frac{C_1}{p^{2e+1}} + O(\frac{1}{p^{2e + 2d +2}} ) \leq \frac{C_3}{p^{2e+1}}$ for all $m$.

 We now sum both sides of \autoref{eqn.Fsigexistscomputation} over all $m$. Note that the terms of this sum are non-zero only for $m \leq p\lceil C_0 p^{e} \rceil : = pM$. Thus, the left-hand side of the sum may be written as \[\frac{1}{p^{e(d+1) + 1}}\sum_{m=0}^{pM}\dim_k \frac{H^0(\lfloor \frac{m}{p}\rfloor L)}{I_e(\lfloor \frac{m}{p} \rfloor L)} = \frac{p}{p^{e(d+1) + 1}} \sum_{m=0}^{M}\dim_k \frac{H^0(mL)}{I_e(mL)} = \frac{a_e}{p^{e(d+1)}}\]
 On the other hand, summing up the right-hand side of \autoref{eqn.Fsigexistscomputation} over $m = 0, \dots, Mp$, we have
\[\begin{split}  \frac{1}{p^{(e+1)(d+1)}}\sum_{m=0}^{Mp}\dim_k \frac{H^0(mL)}{I_{e+1}(mL)} +\sum_{m=0}^{Mp}
\frac{C_3}{p^{2e+1}} & =\frac{a_{e+1}}{p^{(e+1)(d+1)}} +
\frac{C_3(Mp+1)}{p^{2e+1}} \\  \leq \frac{a_{e+1}}{p^{(e+1)(d+1)}}+ \frac{C_3 (C_0 p^{e+1} + p)}{p^{2e+1}} & \leq \frac{a_{e+1}}{p^{(e+1)(d+1)}}+ \frac{2C_0C_3}{p^{e}}. \end{split}\]
Hence, we have shown that for all $e \geq 1$, we have \[\frac{a_e}{p^{e(d+1)}}\leq \frac{a_{e+1}}{p^{(e+1)(d+1)}} + \frac{C}{p^e}\]
where $C = 2 C_0 C_3$. Applying \autoref{Lem.LimitExists} completes the proof that the limit defining $\mathscr{s}_X(L)$ exists.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- pn-2: body_md -->
\label{Pn:TransformationRuleFsig}
    Let $X$ be a normal projective variety over $k$ and $L$ be a big Cartier divisor on $X$. Then, for any integer $n \geq 1$, we have the transformation rule
    \[ \mathscr{s}_X(L^n) = \frac{\mathscr{s}_X(L)}{n}.\]
<!-- end pn-2 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
The case $n=1$ is immediate, so we may assume $n\geq 2$. To show the identity, we will rearrange the sums as follows. \[\sum_{m=0}^\infty \dim_k\frac{H^0(mL)}{I_e(mL)} = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\sum_{q=0}^{\infty}\dim_k\frac{H^0(nqL + iL)}{I_e(nqL+iL)}\]
By \autoref{Pn:twistedFsig}, for each $i = 1,2, \dots, n-1$, there exists a constant $C_{i}>0$ such that \[\left|\dim_k\frac{H^0(nqL+iL)}{I_e(nqL+iL)}-\dim _k\frac{H^0(nqL)}{I_e(nqL)}\right| < C_{i} p^{e(\dim (X) -1)}\] for all $e>0, m\geq0$. Let $\tilde{C} = \max{C_i}$. Furthermore, by \autoref{Thm:DegenSpaceEqualsWholeSpace}, there is a constant $C$ such that $H^0(nqL) = I_e(nqL)$ and $H^0(nqL+iL) = I_e(nqL+iL)$ for all $q>Cp^e/n$ and $i=0,\dots, n-1$. Hence,
\[\begin{split} &\left|\sum_{m=0}^{\infty} \dim_k\frac{H^0(mL)}{I_e(mL)}-n\sum_{m=0}^{\infty} \dim_k\frac{H^0(mnL)}{I_e(mnL)}\right|\\
=&\left|\left(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\sum_{q=0}^{\infty} \dim_k\frac{H^0(nqL+iL)}{I_e(nqL+iL)}-\dim_k\frac{H^0(nqL)}{I_e(nqL)}\right)\right|\\
\leq & \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\sum_{q=0}^{\lfloor Cp^e/n\rfloor} \left|\dim_k\frac{H^0(nqL+iL)}{I_e(nqL+iL)}-\dim_k\frac{H^0(nqL)}{I_e(nqL)}\right| \\
\leq & n \left\lfloor\frac{Cp^e}{n}\right\rfloor\tilde{C}p^{e(\dim(X) -1)} \leq Mp^{e\dim(X)} \text{ for some constant $M>0$.} 
\end{split}\]
Dividing both sides by $p^{e(\dim(X)+1)}$ and taking $e\xrightarrow{\ \ }\infty$ we have \[\mathscr{s}_X(L) -n\mathscr{s}_X(L^{n}) = \lim_{e\xrightarrow{\ \ }\infty}\frac{1}{p^{e(\dim(X)+1)}}\left(\sum_{m=0}^{\infty} \dim_k\frac{H^0(mL)}{I_e(mL)}-n\sum_{m=0}^{\infty} \dim_k\frac{H^0(mnL)}{I_e(mnL)}\right) = 0.\]
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- dfn-10: body_md -->
\label{dfn:FsigofbigQdiv}
Let $X$ be a normal projective variety over $k$ and $L$ be a big $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier $\mathbb {Q}$-divisor. Then, we define \[\mathscr{s}_X(L):=r\mathscr{s}_X(L^r)\]
for any $r > 0$ such that $rL$ is a Cartier divisor. This is well-defined by \autoref{Pn:TransformationRuleFsig}.
<!-- end dfn-10 -->
<!-- rem-3: body_md -->
We will prove in \autoref{thm:positivityofFsigbig} that a normal projective variety $X$ is globally $F$-regular if and only if the $F$-signature $\mathscr{s}_X (L)$ is positive for \emph{some} (equivalently, any) big divisor $L$.
<!-- end rem-3 -->
<!-- rem-4: body_md -->
If $X$ is globally $F$-regular, then there are no numerically trivial $\mbox{$\mathbb{Z}$}$ or $\mathbb{Q}$-divisors over $X$. In other words, numerical equivalence on $X$ is the same as linear equivalence \cite[Theorem 3.4]{LeePandeFsigAmpCone}. Hence, we regard the $F$-signature function $\mathscr{s}_X$ as a well-defined function on the rational big cone of $X$.
<!-- end rem-4 -->
<!-- pn-3: body_md -->
\label{Prop:signaturevolumecomparison}
Let $X$ be a $d$-dimensional normal globally $F$-regular variety over $k$. Fix a norm $\| \cdot \|$ on the N\'eron-Severi space of $X$. Then, there exists a constant $C$ such that for any big $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $L$, \[ \mathscr{s}_X(L) \leq \frac{C\mathrm{vol}(L)}{\|L\|^{d+1}}.\]
<!-- end pn-3 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
It suffices to show the existence of such $C$ for integral big divisors due to the transformation rule. By \autoref{Thm:DegenSpaceEqualsWholeSpace}, there exists $C_1>0$ such that for any big divisor $L$, $I_e(mL) = H^0(mL)$ for all $m>\frac{Cp^e}{\|L\|}.$ Hence, we may write 
\[\begin{split} \mathscr{s}_X(L) & = \lim_{e\xrightarrow{\ \ }\infty}\frac{1}{p^{e(d+1)}}\sum_{m=0}^\infty \dim_k\frac{H^0(mL)}{I_e(mL)}\\ & = \lim_{e\xrightarrow{\ \ }\infty} \frac{1}{p^{e(d+1)}}\sum_{m=0}^{\lfloor C_1p^e/\|L\|\rfloor}\dim_k\frac{H^0(mL)}{I_e(mL)} \\ &\leq \lim_{e\xrightarrow{\ \ }\infty}\frac{1}{p^{e(d+1)}}\sum_{m=0}^{\lfloor C_1p^e/\|L\|\rfloor}\dim_k H^0(mL) \\ &\leq \lim_{N\xrightarrow{\ \ }\infty} \frac{C_1^{d+1}}{N^{d+1}\|L\|^{d+1}}\sum_{m=0}^N\dim_k H^0(mL) \\ & = \frac{C_1^{d+1}}{(d+1)!\|L\|^{d+1}}\mathrm{vol}(L) \text{ (by \autoref{lem:sumvol}).}\end{split}\]
Therefore, the theorem follows.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- thm-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:FsigLocallyLipschitz}
Let $X$ be a globally $F$-regular projective variety over $k$. There is a well-defined and continuous $F$-signature function on the big cone of $X$
\[ \mathscr{s}_X: \text{Big} (X) \xrightarrow{\ \ } \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\]
extending \autoref{dfn:FsigofbigQdiv} on big $\mathbb{Q}$-divisors and the $F$-signature function from \cite{LeePandeFsigAmpCone} on the ample cone. Moreover, $\mathscr{s}_X$ is locally Lipschitz continuous extension on the big cone satisfies the identity $\mathscr{s}_X( tL) = \frac{\mathscr{s}_X (L)}{t}$ for all $t >0$ and $L \in \text{Big} (X)$. Furthermore, for any closed cone $\mathcal{C}\subseteq N^1(X)_\mathbb{R}$ with $\mathcal{C}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq \mathrm{Big}(X)$, there exists $M$ such that 
\[|\mathscr{s}_X(L)-\mathscr{s}_X(L')|\leq \frac{M}{\min\{\|L\|,\|L'\|\}^2}\|L-L'\|\] for all nonzero $L,L'\in\mathcal{C}$.
In particular, for any $\epsilon>0$, the $F$-signature function is Lipschitz continuous on $\{L\in\mathcal{C}\mid \|L\|\geq \epsilon\}$.
<!-- end thm-3 -->
<!-- not-1: body_md -->
We denote $C\subseteq \mathbb{R}^k$ as \emph{a pointed convex cone} if it satisfies 
\begin{itemize} 
\item $\mathrm{int}(C)$ is not empty
\item for each $x\in C$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}$, $\lambda x\in C$
\item for each $x,y\in C$, $x+y\in C$
\item $\bar{C}\cap (-\bar{C}) = \{0\}$ where $\bar{C}$ is the closure of $C$.
\end{itemize} Furthermore, we denote $C_\mathbb{Q} := C\cap \mathbb{Q}^k$ be rational points in $C$.
<!-- end not-1 -->
<!-- lem-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:LipschitzContinuousExtension}
Let $C\subset \mathbb{R}^k$ be an open pointed convex cone and $\| \|$ be a fixed norm on $\mathbb{R}^k$. Let $f:C_\mathbb{Q}\xrightarrow{\ \ } \mathbb{R}$ be a function defined on nonzero rational points on $C$ such that for each real $z\in C$, there exist constants $A(z)>0$ and $R(z)>0$ such that if $x,y\in C_\mathbb{Q}\cap B_{R(z)}(z)$ with $x-y\in C$, then \[|f(x)-f(y)| < A(z)\|x-y\|.\] Then, $f$ is locally Lipschitz continuous on $C$ (i.e., even when $x-y$ is not contained in $\mathrm{int}(C)$). As a consequence $f$ admits a unique continuous extension $\tilde f:C\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ and this extension is locally Lipschitz.
<!-- end lem-8 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
Let $z\in C$. We aim to shrink $R(z)$ so that $f$ is locally Lipschitz in every direction. Fix $z_0\in C_\mathbb{Q}$ a rational point in the cone. Consider $\epsilon >0$ such that $B_\epsilon(z_0)\subseteq C$. Let $K=1+\frac{4\|z_0\|}{\epsilon}$ and $r(z) := \frac{R(z)}{2K}$. Now, we take arbitrary two rational points $x,y\in B_{r(z)}(z)\cap C_\mathbb{Q}$. We choose a rational number $t$ such that $\frac{\|x-y\|}{\epsilon} < t < \frac{2\|x-y\|}{\epsilon}.$ Now, set $w=x+tz_0$ a rational point. Here, $w\in B_{R(z)}(z)$ since \[\begin{split}\|w-z\| = \|x+tz_0 -z\| &\leq \|x-z\| + t\|z_0\|\\
&\leq \|x-z\| + \frac{2\|x-y\|}{\epsilon}\|z_0\|\\
&\leq r(z)+\frac{4r(z)}{\epsilon}\|z_0\| \\ 
& = r(z) K = \frac{R(z)}{2}.
\end{split}\] Furthermore, we can observe that both $w-x$ and $w-y$ are in $C_\mathbb{Q}$. In particular, we see $w-y = t((x-y)/t + z_0)$ and $(x-y)/t + z_0 \in B_{\epsilon}(z_0)\subseteq C$. Hence, by the assumption, 
\[\begin{split}|f(x)-f(y)| & \leq |f(x)-f(w)|+|f(w)-f(y)|\\
& \leq A(z)\|x-w\| + A(z) \|w-y\| \\ 
& \leq A(z) \left( t\|z_0\| + \|x-y\| + t\|z_0\|\right) \\
& \leq A(z) \left(\frac{4\|x-y\|}{\epsilon}\|z_0\| + \|x-y\|\right) \\ 
& = A(z)K\|x-y\|.
\end{split}\] Therefore, the claim follows.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- pn-4: body_md -->
\label{Pn:LocallyLipschitzwithTransformationRule}
Assume the hypotheses of \autoref{lem:LipschitzContinuousExtension}. Furthermore, assume $f(tx)=\frac{1}{t}f(x)$ for any $x\in C_\mathbb{Q}$ and any positive rational number $t$. Then, its continuous extension also satisfy $\tilde{f}(tx) = \frac{1}{t}\tilde{f}(x)$ for any $x\in C$ and $t>0$. Furthermore, let $\mathcal{C}\subseteq \mathbb{R}^k$ be a closed cone such that $\mathcal{C}\setminus{\{0\}}\subseteq C$. Then, there exist $R>0$ and $M>0$ such that for every $z\in \mathcal{C}\setminus{\{0\}}$, $B_{R\|z\|}(z) \subseteq C$ and \[|\tilde{f}(x)-\tilde{f}(y)|\leq \frac{M}{\|z\|^2}\|x-y\|\] for any $x,y\in B_{R\|z\|}(z)$.
<!-- end pn-4 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
The continuous extension admits the transformation since $\tilde{f}$ is continuous. Now, consider a compact subset \[\kappa=\{\xi \in \mathcal{C}\mid 1 \leq \| \xi \| \leq 2\}.\] By \autoref{lem:LipschitzContinuousExtension}, there exists $K>0$ such that for any $\xi \in \kappa$, we can find $r(\xi)$  such that $\tilde{f}$ is Lipschitz continuous on $B_{r(\xi)}(\xi)$ with a Lipschitz constant $KA(\xi)$. Here, since $\cup B_{r(\xi)/2}(\xi)$ covers $\kappa$ and $\kappa$ is compact, we can find a finite subcover with centers $\xi_1,\dots ,\xi_N$. Let $R= \frac{1}{2}\min r(\xi_i)$ and $M = K\max A(\xi_i)$. Now, take any $z\in \mathcal{C}\setminus\{0\}.$ Let $w = z/\|z\|$ be the normalization of $z$. Since $w\in \kappa$, $w$ is in $B_{r(\xi_i)/2}(\xi_i)$ for some $i$. Therefore, we have $B_R(w)\subseteq B_{r(\xi_i)}(\xi_i)$. With this, consider arbitrary two elements $x,y\in B_{R\|z\|}(z)$. Then, \[\begin{split}|\tilde{f}(x)-\tilde{f}(y)|&=\frac{1}{\|z\|}\left|\tilde{f}\left(\frac{x}{\|z\|}\right)-\tilde{f}\left(\frac{y}{\|z\|}\right)\right|\\
& \leq \frac{1}{\|z\|}M\left\|\frac{x}{\|z\|} - \frac{y}{\|z\|}\right\| \\
& = \frac{M}{\|z\|^2}\|x-y\|.
\end{split}
\] Therefore, the theorem follows.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- thm-4: body_md -->
\label{Thm:LipschitzAwayFromZero}
With the hypothesis as \autoref{Pn:LocallyLipschitzwithTransformationRule}, there is a constant $\tilde{M}>0$ such that for any $x,y\in \mathcal{C}\setminus\{0\}$, \[|\tilde{f}(x)-\tilde{f}(y)| \leq \frac{\tilde{M}}{\min\{\|x\|,\|y\|\}^2}\|x-y\|.\] As a consequence $\tilde{f}$ is Lipschitz continuous on $\{x\in \mathcal{C}\mid \|x\|\geq \epsilon \}$ for any $\epsilon>0$.
<!-- end thm-4 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Let $L=\{\xi \in \mathcal{C} \mid \|\xi \| =1\}$ be a compact subset of $C$. Let $B = \max_{u\in L}|\tilde{f}(u)|$. Here, due to the transformation rule, we may observe $|\tilde{f}(x)| = \frac{|\tilde{f}(x/\|x\|)|}{\|x\|}\leq B/\|x\|$ for any $x\in \mathcal{C}\setminus\{0\}.$ Now, to prove the theorem, consider two arbitrary elements $x,y\in \mathcal{C}\setminus\{0\}$. Without loss of generality, assume $\|x\|\leq \|y\|$. Now, suppose that $\|x-y\| <R\|x\|$. Then, by \autoref{Pn:LocallyLipschitzwithTransformationRule}, if we set $z = x$, we have \[ |\tilde{f}(x)-\tilde{f}(y)|\leq \frac{M}{\|x\|^2}\|x-y\|=\frac{M}{\min\{\|x\|,\|y\|\}^2}\|x-y\|\] We note here that this $M$ is independent of the choice of $x$ and $y$. On the other hand, if $\|x-y\|\geq R\|x\|$, we have \[|\tilde{f}(x)-\tilde{f}(y)|\leq \frac{B}{\|x\|}+\frac{B}{\|y\|} \leq \frac{2B}{\min\{\|x\|,\|y\|\}}\leq \frac{2B}{R\min\{\|x\|,\|y\|\}^2}\|x-y\|.\] Here, $B$ and $R$ are also independent to $x$ and $y$. Hence taking $\tilde{M}=\max\{M,2B/R\}$ proves the theorem.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- lem-9: body_md -->
\label{lem.BoundsForFsigBigDiv}(cf. \cite{LeePandeFsigAmpCone})
Let $X$ be a $d$-dimensional normal variety over $k$. Let $L$ be a big Cartier divisor and $H$ be an effective Cartier divisor on $X$. Let $n$ and $b:=b(n)$ (depending only on $n$) be positive integers such that $n>2\|H\|/\|L\|$ and that $nL-bH$ is big. Then, there exists a constant $C$ depending only on $X$ such that \[\left|\mathscr{s}_X(L) - \mathscr{s}_X\left(L+\frac{1}{n}H\right)\right|\leq \frac{C}{\|L\|^{d+1}}\left(2\mathrm{vol}(L)\frac{(b+1)^d - b^d}{b^d} + \mathrm{vol}\left(L+\frac{1}{n}H\right)-\mathrm{vol}(L)\right) + 2\frac{\mathscr{s}_X(L)}{b+1}.\]
<!-- end lem-9 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
By \autoref{MainthmA}, we know the $F$-signature exists. Thus, the inequality follows from the dimension computations of the non-splitting subspaces of the global sections from the proof of \cite[Lemma 4.14]{LeePandeFsigAmpCone}. We omit the computations here.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
By \autoref{Pn:TransformationRuleFsig}, the $F$-signature function has the transformation rule $\mathscr{s}_X(L^n) = \frac{1}{n}\mathscr{s}_X(L)$ for any $n\in \mathbb{N}$ and a big divisor $L$. The transformation rule naturally extends to positive rational numbers. To show the $F$-signature function is locally Lipschitz continuous on the big cone, it remains to show that the difference is bounded when we move in an effective direction. 

Let $D\in \mathrm{Big}(X)$ be a real big divisor class. Since the big cone is open, there exists a constant $r>0$ such that $\overline{B_{2r}(D)}\subseteq \mathrm{Big}(X)$ and $r<\frac{\|D\|}{2}$. Consider big $\mathbb{Q}$-divisors $L$ and $L'$ in $B_{r/4}(D)$ such that $L'-L$ is big. Then, we may observe \[ \|L'-L\| \leq \|L'-D\|+\|L-D\| \leq \frac{r}{2}.\]
Furthermore, we also have \begin{equation}\label{eqn:lowerboundforL} \|L\| \geq \|D\|-\|L-D\|\geq 2r-\frac{r}{4}=\frac{7}{4}r.\end{equation}
Hence, $L$ and $L'$ are big $\mathbb{Q}$-divisors such that $\|L'-L\| < \frac{\|L\|}{2}$ and that $L'-L$ is big. Now, let us write $L'-L = \frac{1}{n}H$ for some large $n\in \mathbb{N}$ where $H$ is an effective divisor. Let $b(n) := \lfloor \frac{nr}{\|H\|}\rfloor$ so that $b(n)\xrightarrow{\ \ } \infty$ as $n\xrightarrow{\ \ } \infty$. Furthermore, by construction, $2\frac{\|H\|}{\|L\|} = n\frac{2\|L'-L\|}{\|L\|} < n$ and $nL-bH$ is big. Indeed, we observe $L-\frac{b}{n}H\in B_{2r}(D)$ since \[\left\|D-\left(L-\frac{b}{n}H\right) \right\|\leq \|D-L\| + \frac{b}{n}\|H\|\leq \frac{r}{4}+r < 2r.\] 
Now, by \autoref{lem.BoundsForFsigBigDiv}, 
\[\begin{split}\left|\mathscr{s}_X(L) - \mathscr{s}_X\left(L+\frac{1}{n}H\right)\right|&\leq \frac{C}{\|L\|^{d+1}}\left(2\mathrm{vol}(L)\frac{(b+1)^d - b^d}{b^d} + \mathrm{vol}\left(L+\frac{1}{n}H\right)-\mathrm{vol}(L)\right) + 2\frac{\mathscr{s}_X(L)}{b+1}\\ 
 &\leq \frac{C}{\|L\|^{d+1}}\left(2\mathrm{vol}(L)\frac{2^d}{b} + \mathrm{vol}\left(L+\frac{1}{n}H\right)-\mathrm{vol}(L)\right) + \frac{2}{b}\mathscr{s}_X(L)\\
\end{split}
\] Now, note that for any big $\mathbb{Q}$-divisors $L_1$ and $L_2$, \[|\mathrm{vol}(L_1) - \mathrm{vol}(L_2)|\leq C_0 \max (\|L_1\|, \|L_2\|)^{d-1} \|L_1 - L_2\|\] for some constant $C_0$ depending only on $X$ and the norm $\| \|$. Here, recall that we picked $L,L'\in B_{r/4}(D)$ where $r<\frac{\|D\|}{4}$. Hence, both $\|L\|$ and $\|L'\|$ are less than $2\|D\|$. Further, $b(n) := \lfloor \frac{nr}{\|H\|}\rfloor\geq \frac{nr}{2\|H\|}$. If we substitute $H = n(L'-L)$ and all information we had above, the inequality becomes 
\[\begin{split}|\mathscr{s}_X(L)-\mathscr{s}_X(L')| & \leq \frac{C}{\|L\|^{d+1}}\left(\frac{2^{d+2}}{r}\mathrm{vol}(L)\|L-L'\| + 2^{d-1}C_0 \|D\|^{d-1} \|L-L'\|\right) + \frac{4}{r}\mathscr{s}_X(L)\|L-L'\|\\
& \leq \left(\frac{C}{\|L\|^{d+1}}\left(\frac{2^{d+2}}{r}\mathrm{vol}(L)+2^{d-1}\|D\|^{d-1}C_0\right) + \frac{4}{r}\mathscr{s}_X(L)\right) \|L-L'\|.
\end{split}\] 
Now, \autoref{Prop:signaturevolumecomparison}, 
$\mathscr{s}_X(L)\leq C_1\frac{\mathrm{vol}(L)}{\|L\|^{d+1}}$ for some uniform constant $C_1$. Furthermore, the volume function is continuous on the big cone, so we let $M=\max_{L\in \overline{B_{2r}(D)}}\mathrm{vol}(L)$. By \autoref{eqn:lowerboundforL}, we have $\|L\|\geq \frac{7}{4}r$. Hence, \[|\mathscr{s}_X(L)-\mathscr{s}_X(L')| \leq \left(C\left(\frac{4}{7r}\right)^{d+1}\left(\frac{2^{d+2}M}{r}+2^{d-1}\|D\|^{d-1}C_0\right)+7C_1M\left(\frac{4}{7r}\right)^{d+2}\right)\|L-L'\|.\]
Here, the Lipschitz constant on the above inequality depends only on $\|D\|$. Indeed $C$ and $C_0$ are independent to the divisors we chose. $r$ and $M$ are constants depend only $D$. 

Therefore, by \autoref{lem:LipschitzContinuousExtension}, the $F$-signature function is locally Lipschitz continuous on the big cone and admits the continuous extension to the big cone. By \autoref{Thm:LipschitzAwayFromZero}, there exists $M$ such that \[|\mathscr{s}_X(L)-\mathscr{s}_X(L')|\leq \frac{M}{\min\{\|L\|,\|L'\|\}^2}\|L-L'\|.\]
As a consequence, we conclude that the $F$-signature function is Lipschitz continuous on $\{L\in \mathcal{C} \mid \|x\| \geq \epsilon\}$ where $\epsilon >0$ is a positive number and  $\mathcal{C}$ is a closed cone such that $\mathcal{C}\setminus\{0\}\subset \mathrm{Big}(X)$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- dfn-11: body_md -->
\label{alphae}
 Let $L$ be a big Cartier divisor on $X$. For each integer $e \geq 1$, we define
\[ m_{e} (X, L) : = \max \left(\{ m \geq 0 \, | \, I_{e} (mL)  = 0 \}\cup\{0\}\right), \]
where $I_e$ is the subspace defined in \autoref{Iedfn}. We also define
\[ \alpha_{e}(X,L) := \frac{m_e (X,L)}{p^e} .\]
<!-- end dfn-11 -->
<!-- lem-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:AlphaInvExists}
     The limit $\lim_{e \xrightarrow{\ \ } \infty} \alpha_e (X,L)$ exists.
<!-- end lem-10 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
We first claim that for all $e \geq 1$, we have
     \begin{equation}\label{monotonicity} \alpha_{e}  + \frac{1}{p^e} \geq \alpha_{e+1}  + \frac{1}{p^{e+1}}. \end{equation}
     Let $0  \neq f $ be an element of $I_e (m_e + 1)$ (which exists by definition). Then, we have that $f^{p} $ is a non-zero element of $I_{e+1} (p(m_e + 1))$ (see \cite[Lemma 3.11]{PandeFrobeniusVersionTiansAlphaInvariant}). In other words, $I_{e+1}(p(m_e+1))\neq 0$. Hence, it implies
    \[ p(m_e +1) \geq m_{e+1} + 1. \]
    Dividing both sides by $p^{e+1}$, we obtain the inequality \autoref{monotonicity}.
   Therefore, the sequence $\{ \alpha_e + \frac{1}{p^e} \}_{e \geq 1}$ is decreasing sequence of non-negative real numbers. Hence, the sequence converges to its infimum. Moreover, since the sequence $\frac{1}{p^{e}}$ converges to zero, the sequence $\{ \alpha_e \}_{e \geq 1}$ also converges and
   \[ \lim _{e \xrightarrow{\ \ } \infty} \alpha_{e} = \inf _{e \geq 1} \{ \alpha_e + \frac{1}{p^e} \}. \]
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- dfn-12: body_md -->
\label{Falphadfn}
    We define the $\alpha_{F}$-invariant of $(X,L)$ as
    \[ \alpha_{F}(X,L) := \lim_{e \xrightarrow{\ \ } \infty} \alpha_e (X,L).\]
<!-- end dfn-12 -->
<!-- rem-5: body_md -->
When $L$ is an ample divisor, this definition of $\alpha_{F}$-invariant can be interpreted in terms of $F$-pure thresholds and is an analog of Tian's $\alpha$-invariant in positive characteristics \cite{PandeFrobeniusVersionTiansAlphaInvariant}.
<!-- end rem-5 -->
<!-- pn-5: body_md -->
\cite{PandeFrobeniusVersionTiansAlphaInvariant} \label{Prop:transformationforalpha}
Let $X$ be a normal projective variety, and $L$ be a big Cartier divisor. Then, for any $n\geq 1$, \[\alpha_F(X,nL) = \frac{1}{n}\alpha_F(X,L)\]
<!-- end pn-5 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
Fix $M\gg0$ such that $| mL| \not= 0$ for all $m\geq M$. We claim $m_e(L) \leq nm_e(nL)\leq m_e(L) + M$. For the first inequality, it suffices to show $ \lfloor m_e(L)/n \rfloor \leq m_e(nL)$ since $m_e$'s are integers. This follows from the definition since $n\lfloor m_e(L) / n\rfloor \leq m_e(L)$, which implies $I_e(n\lfloor m_e(L)/n\rfloor L) = 0$. Now, we prove $nm_e(nL) \leq m_e(L)+ M$. We may assume $nm_e(nL) - M >0$. If not, we have $nm_e(nL) - M \leq m_e(L)$ that already gives the required inequality.

Set $k = nm_e(L) - M$. Since $M\leq nm_e(nL) - k$, we have $|(nm_e(nL) - k)L|\not=\emptyset$. Hence, we can take an effective divisor $E\in |(nm_e(nL) - k)L|$ such that $kL + E\sim nm_e(nL)L$. By construction, we have $I_e(kL+E) = 0$. Now, since $I_e(kL) \subseteq I_e(kL+E)$, we have $I_e(kL) = 0$, or equivalently, $k\leq m_e(L)$. Therefore, $nm_e(L) - M \leq m_e(L)$. Now, dividing the inequality by $1/p^e$ and take the limit $e\xrightarrow{\ \ } \infty$, we have $\alpha_F(X, nL) = \frac{1}{n}\alpha_F(X,L)$.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- dfn-13: body_md -->
\label{dfn:alphaofQQdiv}
    Let $X$ be a normal projective variety over $k$ and $L$ be a big, $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier, $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor. Then, we define $\alpha_{F}(X,L) $ by the formula
    \[ \alpha_{F}(X,L) = n \, \alpha_{F}(X,nL)  \]
    where $n \geq 1$ is any integer such that $nL$ is a Cartier divisor. Thanks to \autoref{Prop:transformationforalpha}, the definition of $\alpha_{F}(X,L)$ is independent of the choice of $n$.
<!-- end dfn-13 -->
<!-- pn-6: body_md -->
\label{Prop:addingeffective}
    Let $X$ be a normal projective variety and $L$ be a big $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier divisor on $X$. Let $E$ be any effective $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier divisor on $X$. Then we have
 \[ \alpha_{F}(X,L) \geq \alpha_{F}(X, L+E) .\]
<!-- end pn-6 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Let $n$ and $m$ be the Cartier index of $L$ and $E$ respectively. Let $L'= mnL$ and $E'=mnE$. Using \autoref{lem:Ieeffective}, we see that for any $e \geq 1$, we have $m_e (X,L') \geq m_e (X, L'+E')$. Now, the proposition follows from \autoref{Prop:transformationforalpha} and the definition of $\alpha_{F}$-invariant.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- pn-7: body_md -->
\label{Prop:Fsigandalphacomparison}
    Let $X$ be a normal, projective variety and $L$ be a big Cartier divisor. Assume that $d = \dim(X)$ is positive. Fix a constant $C>0$ such that for all $e \geq 1$ and all $m \geq C p^e$, we have $I_e (mL) = H^0 (mL)$. Then, we have the inequality
    \[ \frac{\mathrm{vol}(L) \, \alpha_{F}(X, L)^{d+1}}{(d+1)!} \leq  \mathscr{s}_X(L) \leq \frac{\mathrm{vol}(L)}{(d+1)!} \, \big( C^{d+1} - (C - \alpha_{F}(X,L) )^{d+1} \big) . \]
<!-- end pn-7 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
The first inequality follows immediately from the definition of the $F$-signature of $L$, once we use the fact that for any $e \geq 1$, $I_e (m) = 0$ for $m \leq m_{e}(X,L)$ (see \autoref{alphae}). For the second inequality, we use \autoref{postivitylemma} proved below along with the fact that for any real number $\lambda > \alpha_{F}(X,L)$, there exists an $e \gg 1 $ and a section $f \in I_e (nL)$ such that $\lambda > \frac{n}{p^e -1 }$. The inequality then follows by taking a limit $\lambda \xrightarrow{\ \ } \alpha_{F}(X,L)$.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- lem-11: body_md -->
\cite[Lemma 4.7] {PandeFrobeniusVersionTiansAlphaInvariant} \label{postivitylemma}
Fix a constant $C>0$ such that for all $e \geq 1$ and all $m \geq C p^e$, we have $I_e (mL) = 0$. Suppose we have integers $e_0,n \geq 1$ and a non-zero section $f \in I_{e_0} (nL) \subset H^0 (X, \mathcal O_X (nL))$ and set $\lambda \geq  \frac{n}{p^{e_0} - 1} $ be any real number. Then,
  \begin{equation}
        \mathscr{s}_X(L) \leq  \frac{\mathrm{vol}(L)}{(d+1)!} \, \big( C^{d+1} - (C - \lambda) ^{d+1} \big) .
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lem-11 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Since $f $ belongs to $I_{e_{0}} (nL)$, for each $ m \geq n$ we know that $f \cdot H^ 0 (X, \mathcal O_X ((m -n) L)) \subset H^0 (X, \mathcal O_X (mL))$ is contained in $ I_{e_{0}}(mL)$ yielding the inequality
\begin{equation}
  \dim_{k} \frac{H^ 0 (X, \mathcal O_X (mL))}{I_{e_{0}}(mL)} \leq  h^ 0 (X, \mathcal O_X (mL)) - h^ 0 (X, \mathcal O_X ((m- n)L))  .  
\end{equation}
for all $m \geq n$.
Further, setting $v_{r} = \frac{p^{re_{0}} }{p^{e_0} - 1} $ for any positive integer $r$, we claim that $f^{v_r} $ belongs to  $I_{re_{0}}(n v_{r} L )$. To see this, let $D$ denote the effective divisor corresponding to $f$ and note that we have a natural map of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal O_X \xrightarrow{\ \ } F_* ^{e_0} (\mathcal O_X (D)) $. Twisting this by $D$ and applying $F_* ^{e_0}$, we obtain a composition:
\[ \mathcal O_X \xrightarrow{\ \ } F_* ^{e_0} \mathcal O_X (D) \xrightarrow{\ \ } F_* ^{2e_0} \mathcal O_X(( 1+ p^{e_0}) D) \]
where the composite map is the same as the composition $\mathcal O_X \xrightarrow{\ \ } F_* ^{2e_0} \xrightarrow{\ \ } F_* ^{2e_0} \mathcal O_X ((p^{e_0} + 1) D)$. Proceeding inductively, we obtain a factorization
\[ \mathcal O_X \xrightarrow{\ \ } F_* ^{e_0} \mathcal O_X ( D) \xrightarrow{\ \ } F_* ^{re_0} \mathcal O_X (v_r D). \]
Therefore, any splitting of the map $\mathcal O_X \xrightarrow{\ \ } F_* ^{re_0} \mathcal O_X (v_r D)$ as provides a splitting of $ \mathcal O_X \xrightarrow{\ \ } F_* ^{e_0} \mathcal O_X ( D) $. This shows that $f^{v_r} \in I_{re_0} (nv_r  L)$.

Therefore, we have
\begin{equation} \label{upperboundinequality}
  \dim_{k} \frac{H^ 0 (X, \mathcal O_X (mL))}{I_{ne_{0}}(m)} \leq h^0 (X, \mathcal O_X(mL)) - h^0 (X, \mathcal O_X((m-nv_{r}) L) )  
\end{equation}
for all $m \geq n v_{r}$. Then, using the \autoref{Dfn.FsigBigDivisors} we may bound the $F$-signature $\mathscr{s}_X(L)$ as follows:
$$ \mathscr{s}_X(L) =  \lim _{r \xrightarrow{\ \ } \infty } \frac{  \sum \limits _{m = 0} ^{ Cp^{re_{0}}} \dim_{k} \frac{H^0 (mL)}{I_{re_{0}}(mL)}}{p^{re_{0}(d+1)}} \leq \Bigg( \lim _{r \xrightarrow{\ \ } \infty } \frac{  \sum \limits _{m = 0} ^{ Cp^{re_{0}}} h^0 (\mathcal O_X(mL))}{p^{re_{0}(d+1)}} - \frac{  \sum \limits _{m = nv_{r}} ^{ Cp^{re_{0}}} h^0 (\mathcal O_X((m- n v_{r}) L) )}{p^{re_{0} (d+1)}} \Bigg).$$
Finally, calculating the dimensions in the above inequality using \autoref{lem:sumvol},
we obtain
\[    \mathscr{s}_X(L) \leq \frac{\mathrm{vol}(L)}{(d+1)!} \big( C^{d+1} - (C - \frac{n}{p^{e_{0}} -1}) ^{d+1} \big).  \]
The proof of the lemma is now complete by using the fact that $\lambda \geq \frac{n}{p^{e_0} -1}$.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- thm-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:positivityofFsigbig}
    Suppose $X$ is a normal projective variety and $L$ is a big divisor over $X$. Suppose $X$ is globally $F$-regular. Then, both $\alpha_{F}(X,L)$ and $\mathscr{s}_X (L)$ (\autoref{dfn:Fsigbig}) are positive.
    
   Conversely, suppose that the $F$-signature $\mathscr{s}_X (L)$ as defined in \autoref{Dfn.FsigBigDivisors} is positive. Then, $X$ is globally $F$-regular.
<!-- end thm-5 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
First assume that $X$ is globally $F$-regular. Then, by \cite[Theorem 4.6]{PandeFrobeniusVersionTiansAlphaInvariant}, the invariant $\alpha_{F}(X, H)$ is positive for any ample divisor $H$. Pick a very ample divisor $H$ such that $H - L = E$ is linearly equivalent to an effective divisor $E$. Then by \autoref{Prop:addingeffective}, we have $\alpha_{F}(X, L) \geq \alpha_{F}(X, H = L +E) > 0 .$ Therefore, we see that $\alpha_{F} (X, L) >0$. Using \autoref{Prop:Fsigandalphacomparison}, we see that $\mathscr{s}_X (L) > 0$ as well since $\mathrm{vol} (L) >0$ for the big divisor $L$.

    For the converse, we will show that if the $F$-signature of a big divisor $L$ is positive, then the $F$-signature of any ample divisor $H$ over $X$ is positive as well, from which the theorem follows by the local case proved in \cite{AberbachLeuschke}. First, we claim that if $\mathscr{s}_ X(L)$ is positive, then $\alpha_{F}(X,L)$ is positive as well. This follows immediately from \autoref{Prop:Fsigandalphacomparison}. Let $H$ be any ample Cartier divisor on $X$. Since $L$ is assumed to be big, we have $nL - H$ is effective for some $n \gg 0$. Therefore, we may write $nL = H + E$. By the monotonicity (\autoref{Prop:addingeffective}) and the transformation property (\autoref{Prop:transformationforalpha}) of the $\alpha_{F}$-invariant, we obtain
    \[ \alpha_{F}(X,H) \geq \alpha_{F}(X, nL) = \frac{1}{n} \alpha_{F}(X,L) > 0 .\]
    Therefore, we have $\alpha_{F}(X,H) >0 $ and hence by \autoref{Prop:Fsigandalphacomparison} again, we have $\mathscr{s}_X (H) > 0$.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- thm-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:alphaonbigcone}
    Let $X$ be a globally $F$-regular projective variety over $k$. Then, the $\alpha_{F}$-invariant defines a well-defined function $\alpha_{F}(X, \_)$ on the real big cone of $X$
    \[\alpha_{F}(X, \_) : \text{Big}_\mathbb{R}(X) \xrightarrow{\ \ } \mathbb{R}\]
    satisfying the following properties:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\alpha_{F}(X,L)$ is a locally Lipshcitz function of $L$.
        \item For any big rational class $L$, $\alpha_{F}(X,L)$ is the same as defined in \autoref{dfn:alphaofQQdiv}.
        \item For any big real class $L$ and any integer $n \geq 1$, we have $\alpha_{F}(X,nL) = \frac{\alpha_{F}(X,L)}{n}$.
        \item  For any big real class $L$ and any effective class $E$ in $\text{N}^1 _\mathbb{R} (X)$, we have $\alpha_{F}(X,L) \geq \alpha_{F}(X, L+E)$.
        \item For any big real class $L$, we have $\alpha_{F}(X,L)$ is positive.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end thm-6 -->
<!-- lem-12: body_md -->
\label{lem.AlphaInvInequality}
Suppose that there is a number $0 <a<1$ such that $aL+D$ and $aL-D$ are both big. Then,  \[|\alpha_F(X, L) - \alpha_F(X,L+D)| \leq \frac{a}{1-a}\alpha_F(X,L)\]
<!-- end lem-12 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Applying \autoref{Prop:addingeffective}, we have \begin{equation}\label{Eqn.ContinuityofAlphaInv1}\begin{split}\alpha_F(X, L) &= (1+a)\alpha_F(X,(1+a)L)  \\ &= (1+a)\alpha_F(X, (L+D) + (aL-D)) \\ &\leq (1+a) \alpha_F(X,L+D) \end{split}\end{equation} In other words, we have $\alpha_F(X,L) - \alpha_F(X,L+D)\leq a\alpha_F(X,L+D)$.
On the other hand, \begin{equation}\label{Eqn.ContinuityofAlphaInv2}\begin{split}\alpha_F(X, L) &= (1-a)\alpha_F(X,(1-a)L)  \\ &= (1-a)\alpha_F(X, (L+D) - (aL+D)) \\ &\geq (1-a) \alpha_F(X,L+D) \end{split}\end{equation} Combining \autoref{Eqn.ContinuityofAlphaInv1} and \autoref{Eqn.ContinuityofAlphaInv2}, we obtain $|\alpha_F(X, L) - \alpha_F(X,L+D)| \leq a\alpha_F(X,L+D) \leq \frac{a}{1-a}\alpha_F(X,L)$.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- lem-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:upperboundonalpha}
Let $X$ be a normal projective variety over $k$. Fix a norm $\| \, \|$ on the N\'eron-Severi space of $X$. Then there exists a constant $C>0$ (depending only on $X$) such that for all big $\mathbb{Q}$-divisors $L$, we have
\[ \alpha_{F}(X,L) \leq \frac{C}{\|L\| } .\]
<!-- end lem-13 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
By the homogeneity of $\alpha_{F}(X,L)$ (\autoref{Prop:transformationforalpha}), it is sufficient to prove the lemma for all big Cartier divisors $L$. From \cite[Theorem~4.9]{LeePandeFsigAmpCone}, we have a constant $C>0$ such that for all $e>0 $ and all big Cartier divisors $L$, we have $I_e (mL) = H^0 (mL)$ for all $m \geq \frac{Cp^e}{\| L \|}$. In particular, for a fixed big divisor $L$ and for all $e \gg 0$ so that $H^0 (mL) \neq 0$ for $m \geq \frac{Cp^e}{\| L \|}$, we have $m _e (L) \leq \frac{Cp^e}{\| L \|} $. It follows that $\alpha_{F}(X, L) \leq \frac{C}{\|L\|}$ for all big $\mathbb{Q}$-divisors $L$.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- lem-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:Alphainvariantlipschitzeffectivedirection}
Let $X$ be a normal projective variety and $L$ be a big $\mathbb{R}$ divisor. Fix a norm $\| \, \|$ on the N\'eron-Severi space of $X$. Let $L$ be a big $\mathbb{R}$-divisor on $X$ Then, there are constants $C, \delta >0$ depending only on $L$ such that for any two big $\mathbb{Q}$-divisors $L_1, L_2\in B_\delta(L)$ such that $L_2-L_1$ is effective and $\|L_2-L_1\|<\frac{\|L_2\|}{2}$, we have \[|\alpha_F(X, L_1) - \alpha_F(X,L_2)|\leq C \| L_1 - L_2 \|.\]
<!-- end lem-14 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Fix $0<r <\frac{1}{2}\|L\|$ such that $B_r(L) \subseteq \mathrm{Big}(X)$. Let $\delta = \frac{r}{4}$. Let $L_1, L_2\in B_\delta(L)$ be big $\mathbb{Q}$-divisors and $L_2-L_1$ is effective. Let $D= L_2 - L_1$. Note that $L_1+D$ and $L_1-D$ are in $B_{\frac{1}{2}r}(L)$, hence they are both big. Now, we observe that $L_1+\left(1+\frac{r}{4\|D\|}\right)D$ and $L_1-\left(1+\frac{r}{4\|D\|}\right)D$ are in $B_r(L)$ since\[\begin{split}\left\|L_1+\left(1+\frac{r}{4\|D\|}\right)D - L\right\| &\leq \left\|D+\frac{r}{4\|D\|}D\right\| + \|L_1 - L\|\\ & \leq \| D \| +\left\|\frac{r}{4\|D\|}\right\|\|D\|+\|L_1 - L\|\\ &< \frac{1}{2}r + \frac{1}{4}r + \frac{1}{4}r =r \end{split}\] Let $a = \frac{4\|D\|}{r+4\|D\|}$. Then, we have $aL_1-D$ and $aL_1+D$ are big and $0<a<1$. Thus, by \autoref{lem.AlphaInvInequality}, we have \[\begin{split}|\alpha_F(X,L_2) - \alpha_F(X,L_1)| &\leq \frac{a}{1-a}\alpha_F(X,L_1)\\
& = \frac{4}{r}\alpha_F(X,L_1)\|L_2-L_1\|\\ & \leq \frac{4C}{r\|L_1\|}\|L_2-L_1\| \text{ (by \autoref{lem:upperboundonalpha})} \\
& \leq \frac{32C}{7r\|L\|}\|L_2-L_1\|.
\end{split}\] The last inequality is because we had $\|L_1-L\| <\frac{1}{4}r$ and $r<\frac{1}{2}\|L\|$. Hence, $\|L\| = \|L-L_1+L_1\| \leq \|L-L_1 \| + \|L_1\| \leq \frac{1}{8}\|L\| + \|L_1\|$. Thus, we have $\frac{7}{8}\|L\| \leq \|L_1\|$.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- pn-8: body_md -->
\label{Prop:alphacontinuity}
Let $X$ be a normal projective variety and $L$ be a big $\mathbb{R}$ divisor. Fix a norm $\| \, \|$ on the N\'eron-Severi space of $X$. Then, there are constants $C, \delta >0$ such that for any two big $\mathbb{Q}$-divisors $L_1, L_2$ such that $\|L_i - L\| < \delta$ for $i=1,2$, we have \[|\alpha_F(X, L_1) - \alpha_F(X,L_2)|\leq C \| L_1 - L_2 \|.\] 
In other words, the function $\alpha_{F}(X , .)$ is locally Lipschitz around every real big class $L$ in the N\'eron-Severi space.
<!-- end pn-8 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
We know that the Frobenius $\alpha$ invariant satisfies the transformation rule by \autoref{Prop:transformationforalpha}. Furthermore, by \autoref{lem:Alphainvariantlipschitzeffectivedirection}, it is locally Lipschitz continuous in effective directions. By \autoref{lem:LipschitzContinuousExtension}, we conclude that the alpha invariant is locally Lipschitz in any direction.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
For any big $\mathbb{R}$-divisor $L$ on $X$, we may define $\alpha_{F}(X,L)$ by the formula
\[ \alpha_{F}(X,L) = \lim_{m \xrightarrow{\ \ } \infty} \alpha_{F}(X,L_m)  \]
for any sequence of big $\mathbb{Q}$-divisors $L_m$ converging to $L$ in $\text{N}^1 _\mathbb{R} (X)$. By \autoref{Prop:alphacontinuity}, this is well-defined and makes $\alpha_{F}(X,L)$ a locally Lipschitz continuous function of $L$. This proves Parts (a) and (b). Part (c) follows from the continuity of $\alpha_{F}(X,L)$ and \autoref{Prop:transformationforalpha}. Similarly, writing both $L$ and $E$ as a limit of big $\mathbb{Q}$-divisors $L_m$ and $E_m$, Part (d) follows from \autoref{Prop:addingeffective}.

For Part (e), we first pick a big $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $L'$ such that $L' - L$ is effective. This can be done by the openness of the big cone. By Part (d), we have that $\alpha_{F}(X,L) \geq \alpha_{F}(X,L')$. Therefore, it is sufficient to show that $\alpha_{F}(X.L')$ is positive. Moreover, by the transformation rule Part (c), we may further assume that $L'$ is a big Cartier divisor. Now pick an ample Cartier divisor $H$ and write $L'+ E  = nH$ for some $n \gg 0$ and an effective Cartier divisor $E$. This can be done since $H$ is ample. Therefore, we have
 \[ \alpha_{F}(X,L') \geq \alpha_{F}(X, L'+ E) = \alpha_{F} (nH) > 0 \]
where in the last inequality we are using the fact that the $\alpha_{F}$-invariant of an ample divisor on a globally $F$-regular projective variety is positive \cite[Theorem~4.6]{PandeFrobeniusVersionTiansAlphaInvariant}. This completes the proof of the theorem.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- thm-7: body_md -->
\label{thm:positivityforbig}
Let $X$ be a normal projective variety over $k$ of positive dimension $d$. Assume that $X$ is globally $F$-regular. Then for any big $\mathbb{R}$-divisor $L$ on $X$, the $F$-signature $\mathscr{s}_X (L)$ is positive. Moreover, for any compact subset $K$ that is contained in the big cone, there exists a constant $C>0$ (depending on $K$) such that $\mathscr{s}_X(L) \geq C \mathrm{vol}(L)$ for all $L  \in K$.
<!-- end thm-7 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
First we note that by using \autoref{Prop:Fsigandalphacomparison} and by continuous extension, for any big $\mathbb{R}$-divisor $L$ we have
    \begin{equation} \label{eqn:Fsigalphainequality} \mathscr{s}_X(L) \geq \frac{\mathrm{vol}(L) \, \alpha_{F}(X, L)^{d+1}}{(d+1)!}.  \end{equation}
    Now, since the function $\alpha_{F}(X,L)$ is positive on the big cone (by Part (e) of \autoref{thm:alphaonbigcone}), the function $\alpha_{F}(X, .)$ achieves a positive minimum on any compact subset contained in the big cone. Choose $M$ to be the minimum value of $\alpha_{F}(X,.)$ on $K$. Then, choosing $C = \frac{M ^{d+1}}{(d+1)!}$ works for the Theorem by \autoref{eqn:Fsigalphainequality}.  The positivity of $\mathscr{s}_X (L)$ now follows from the positivity of $\mathrm{vol}(L)$ since $L$ is assumed to be big.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- rem-6: body_md -->
A special case of the above theorem is that the $F$-signature of ample $\mathbb{R}$-divisors is positive on a globally $F$-regular variety. Even this case of the theorem is new and require the techniques involving the $\alpha_{F}$-invariant developed in this section.
<!-- end rem-6 -->
<!-- dfn-14: body_md -->
\label{gradedsequencedfn}
    Let $X$ be a normal variety over $k$. Then a \emph{graded sequence of ideal sheaves} on $X$, denoted by $\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}$, is a sequence of coherent ideal sheaves $(\mathfrak{a}_n)_{n \geq 1}$ such that for any integers $n,m \geq 1$, we have
    \[ \mathfrak{a}_m \cdot \mathfrak{a}_n \subset \mathfrak{a}_{m+n}.  \]
    In other words, for every affine open set $U \subset X$, the sequence $(\mathfrak{a}_n (U))_{n \geq 1}$ forms a graded sequence of ideals of $\mathcal O_X(U)$. We will follow the convention that $\mathfrak{a}_0 = \mathcal O_X$ for any graded sequence of ideal sheaves $\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}$.
<!-- end dfn-14 -->
<!-- dfn-15: body_md -->
\label{def:gFrforgradedsequence}
Let $X$ be a normal variety over $k$ and $\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}$ be a graded sequence of ideal sheaves on $X$ (\autoref{gradedsequencedfn}). We say that the pair $(X, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$ is \emph{globally $F$-regular} if for any effective Weil divisor $D$, there is an $e > 0$, and an element
\[\varphi\in H^0(F^{e}_{*}\frak{a}_{p^e-1} \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(D),\mathcal O_X))\] 
such that $\varphi(F^e_* 1)=1$, where $F^{e}_{*} 1$ is the global section of $F^{e}_{*}
\mathcal O_X (D)$ that corresponds to the effective divisor $D$. Note that via the natural inclusion
\[ F^e_*\frak{a}_{p^e-1} \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(D),\mathcal O_X)) \subset  \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(D),\mathcal O_X), \]
we may consider any element $\varphi \in H^0(F^{e}_{*}\frak{a}_{p^e-1} \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(D),\mathcal O_X))$, as a map of $\mathcal O_X$-modules from $F^{e}_{*} \mathcal O_X(D)$ to $\mathcal O_X$.
<!-- end dfn-15 -->
<!-- dfn-16: body_md -->
\label{def:Iebullet}
    Let $(X,\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$ be a pair consisting of a normal projective variety $X$ and a graded sequence of ideal sheaves $\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}$. For any Weil divisor $D$ on $X$, we define the subspace $I_e^{\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}}(D)$ as \[I_e^{\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}}(D):= \{f\in H^0(\mathcal O_X (D)) \mid \varphi(F^e_*f) = 0 \text{ for all } \varphi \in H^0(F^e_*\frak{a}_{p^e-1} \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(D),\mathcal O_X)). \}\]
<!-- end dfn-16 -->
<!-- dfn-17: body_md -->
\label{def:fsigofidealsequence}
Let $(X, \mathfrak{a}_\bullet)$ be a pair consisting of a normal projective variety of dimension $d$ and a graded sequence of ideal sheaves $\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}$. We define the $F$-signature function of $\mathscr{s}_X(\mathfrak{a}_\bullet, L)$ for any ample divisor $L$ on $X$ as
\[ \mathscr{s}_X(\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet},L) = \lim_{e \xrightarrow{\ \ }\infty} \frac{1}{p^{e(d+1)}}\sum_{r=0}^\infty \dim \frac{H^0(rL)}{ I^{\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}}_e(rL)}.\]
<!-- end dfn-17 -->
<!-- thm-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:fsigofgradedsequences}
Let $X$ be a normal variety over $k$ and $\mathfrak{a}_\bullet$ be a graded sequence of ideal sheaves on $X$. Let $L$ be an ample divisor on $X$. Then, the $F$-signature $\mathscr{s}_X(\mathfrak{a}_\bullet, L)$ exists and is positive if and only if $(X,\mathfrak{a}_\bullet)$ is globally $F$-regular (\autoref{def:gFrforgradedsequence}).
<!-- end thm-8 -->
<!-- dfn-18: body_md -->
\label{def:globaloperations}
    Given a normal variety $X$ over $k$, we define the following operations on $p^{-e}$-linear maps on $X$:
    \begin{itemize}
       
         \item Given two ideal coherent sheaves $\mathfrak{a}$ and $\mathfrak{b}$, and Weil divisors $D_1$ and $D_2$, and global sections $\varphi$ and $\psi$ of
         $ F^e_*\frak{a} \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(D_1),\mathcal O_X)$ and $ F^f_*\frak{b} \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^f_*\mathcal O_X(D_2),\mathcal O_X)$ respectively, we have the map $\varphi \star \psi \in  F^{e+f} _* (\mathfrak{a} ^{[p^f]} \mathfrak{b}) \cdot( \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^{e+f}_*\mathcal O_X(D_2 + p^f D_1),\mathcal O_X) )$ defined as follows: on any affine open subset $U$ of $X$, we pick local sections $g \in \mathfrak{a}$ and $h \in \mathfrak{b}$ such that $\varphi = \tilde{\varphi} ( F^{e}_{*} g \rule{0.8em}{0.2pt})$ and  $\psi = \tilde{\psi} ( F^f _ * h \rule{0.8em}{0.2pt})$ for maps $\tilde{\varphi} \in \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_U} ( F^{e}_{*} \mathcal O_U (D_1) , \mathcal O_U)$ and $\tilde{\psi} \in \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_U} (F_* ^f \mathcal O_U (D_2) , \mathcal O_U)$, and we define 
         \[ \varphi\star \psi (U) := \tilde{\varphi} \circ F^e_* \big (g\mathcal O_U ( D_1) \otimes_{\mathcal O_U}  \psi  \big )^{**}. \]
        Here $M^{**}$ denotes the reflexification of the module $M$. More concretely, we may first twist the map $\psi$ by the rank one reflexive module $g \mathcal O_U (D_1)$ and reflexify to get a map  
        \[  \big ( g\mathcal O_U ( D_1) \otimes_{\mathcal O_U}   \psi \big )^{**} :  F_* ^{f} \big ( g^{p^f} \,h \, \mathcal O_U (D_2 + p^f D_1) \big ) \xrightarrow{\ \ } g\mathcal O_U (D_1) . \]
       Then, we may pushforward the above map by $F^{e}_{*}$ and post-compose with $\varphi$, which is the resulting map
       \[  \varphi \star \psi (U) : F_* ^{e+f} \big (g^{p^f} \, h \, \mathcal O_U (D_2 + p^f D_1) \big) \xrightarrow{\ \ } F^{e}_{*} (g\mathcal O_U (D_1)) \xrightarrow{\ \ } \mathcal O_X. \]
       This construction naturally globalizes to define a global section $\varphi \star \psi $ of the sheaf  $F^{e+f} _* (\mathfrak{a} ^{[p^f]} \mathfrak{b}) \cdot( \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^{e+f}_*\mathcal O_X(D_2 + p^f D_1),\mathcal O_X) )$.
       \medskip
       
          \item Given a coherent ideal sheaf $\mathfrak{a} \subset \mathcal O_X$ and a Weil divisor $D$ and a global section $\varphi$ of the sheaf
         $ F^e_*\frak{a} \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(D),\mathcal O_X)$ for some $e \geq 1$, we define $\varphi^{[p^f]}$ as the iteratively as $\varphi ^{[p^{f+1}]} = \varphi \star \varphi^{[p^{f}]} $ (for any integer $f \geq 1$). We note that $\varphi ^{[p^f]}$ is naturally a global section of the sheaf $ F^{ef} _* (\mathfrak{a} ^{1 + p^e + \dots + p^{(f-1)e}}) \cdot( \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X( (1 + p^e + \dots + p^{(f-1)e}) D),\mathcal O_X) ) $
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end dfn-18 -->
<!-- pn-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:testdivisor}
    A pair $(X, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$ as in \autoref{def:gFrforgradedsequence} with $X$ \emph{projective} is globally $F$-regular if and only if one of the following conditions hold:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item there exists an ample divisor $L$ on $X$ such that for any $r \geq 0$ and any effective divisor $D \sim r L $, there is an $e > 0$ such that $D \notin I_e ^{\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (rL)$. 

    \item there exists an ample and effective divisor $D_0 \geq 0$ such that:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item  the vanishing locus $ V(\mathfrak{a}_1)$ of $\mathfrak{a}_1$ is contained in the support of $D_0$,

        \item the variety $X \setminus \operatorname{{Supp}} (D_0) $ has strongly $F$-regular singularities and

        \item there is an $e_0 > 0$ such that $D_0 \notin I_{e_0} ^{\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (\mathcal O_X(D_0))$. 
    \end{itemize}
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end pn-9 -->
<!-- lem-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:testdivisor}
    Let $D$ be a Weil divisor on a normal projective variety $X$ and let $f \in H^0 (X, \mathcal O_X (D))$ be a global section. We have the following properties:
    \begin{enumerate}
       \item If $D'$ is another Weil divisor and $g \in H^0 (X, \mathcal O_X (D'))$ such that $fg \notin I_e ^{\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (\mathcal O_X(D + D'))$, then $f \notin I_e ^{\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (\mathcal O_X (D))$.
       

        \item If $f \notin I_{e_0} ^{\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (\mathcal O_X(D))$, then $ f^{1 + p + \dots + p^{e-1}}$ is not contained in $I_{e e_0} ^{\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} ((1 + p + \dots + p^{e-1})D)$ for all $e \geq 1$.

     
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-15 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
Recall the $\star$ and Frobenius-power operations on maps introduced in \autoref{def:globaloperations}.

     \begin{enumerate}
         \item Let $D_f$ and $D_g$ be the effective divisors defined by $f$ and $g$. Note that we have a natural inclusion $\mathcal O_X (D_f ) \subset \mathcal O_X(D_f + D_g)$ (mapping the section $f$ to $fg$) inducing an inclusion
        \[  \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(D_f + D_g),\mathcal O_X)) \subset \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(D_f),\mathcal O_X)). \]
