        By pre-multiplication by sections of $F^{e}_{*} \mathfrak{a}_{p^e -1}$, we then have an inclusion
         \[  F^{e}_{*} \mathfrak{a}_{p^e -1 } \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(D_f + D_g),\mathcal O_X)) \subset F^{e}_{*} \mathfrak{a}_{p^e -1} \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(D_f),\mathcal O_X)). \]
        Then, we see that any element $\psi \in H^0 (F^{e}_{*} \mathfrak{a}_{p^e -1 } \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(D_f + D_g),\mathcal O_X)) $ such that $\psi (F^{e}_{*} 1) = 1$ gives an element $\psi \in H^0 (F^{e}_{*} \mathfrak{a}_{p^e -1} \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(D_f),\mathcal O_X))$ as required.

        \item Let $D_f $ denote the effective Weil divisor corresponding to $f$ (so that $D_f \sim D$). Since $f \notin I_{e_0} ^{\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (\mathcal O_X (D))$, there exists a section $\varphi \in H^0(F^{e_0} _* \mathfrak{a}_{p^{e_0 - 1}} \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F _ *  ^{e_0} \mathcal O_X(D_f),\mathcal O_X)) $ that maps the global section $F_* ^{e_0} 1$ to $1$. Then, it follows from the construction of $\varphi^{[p^e]}$ that it defines a map
        \[ \varphi^{[p^e]}: F^{ee_0}_*\mathcal O_X( (1 + p^{e_0} + \dots + p^{(e-1)e_0} ) D_f),\mathcal O_X)   \]
        such that $ \varphi^{[p^e]} (F_* ^{e e_0} 1)  = 1$ (see \cite[Lemma 5.2.3]{BlickleSchwedeSurveyPMinusE} for a similar argument). Moreover, since $\varphi$ is premultiplied by $\mathfrak{a}_{p^{e_0} -1}$, we have $\varphi ^{[p^e]}  $ is premultiplied by sections of $\mathfrak{a}_{p^{e_0} - 1} ^{\frac{p^{ e e_0  -1}}{p^{e_0} -1}} \subset \mathfrak{a}_{p^{e e_0} - 1}$. This proves part (b) of the lemma. \qedhere
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
The forward direction for both parts follows from the observation that if $(X, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$ is globally $F$-regular, then we know already that $X$ is globally $F$-regular. So we will now prove the converse.
Part (a) of the Proposition follows immediately from Part (a) of \autoref{lem:testdivisor} since for any effective divisor $D$, we may find an $r>0$ and an effective divisor $E$ such that $D + E \sim rL $. 

Now we prove Part (b): We note that since $D_0$ is assumed to be ample, the complement $U = X \setminus \operatorname{{Supp}} (D_0)$ is an affine variety with strongly $F$-regular singularities. Now, for any effective divisor $D \sim r D_0$ (for some $r >0$), we have a splitting $ \phi: F^{e}_{*} \mathcal O_U (D|_U) \xrightarrow{\ \ } \mathcal O_U$ for some $e \gg 0$. We will view $\phi$ as a section of the coherent sheaf $\mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_U}(F^e_*\mathcal O_U(D|_U),\mathcal O_U)$ over the open set $U$ and let $t_0$ denote the section corresponding to $D_0$ of $\mathcal O_X (D_0)$. Since $V(\mathfrak{a}_{p^e - 1})   \subset V (\mathfrak{a}_ 1 ^{p^e -1}) =V(\mathfrak{a}_1) \subset \text{Supp}(D_0) $, we have a restriction map of sections:
\[ H^0 (X,    F^e_*\frak{a}_{p^e -1} \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(D),\mathcal O_X) ) \xrightarrow{\ \ } H^0 (U, \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_U}(F^e_*\mathcal O_U(D|_U),\mathcal O_U)) . \]
Since $U = X \setminus \text{Supp} (D_0)$ and $D_0$ is ample, the section $\phi t_0^n$  extends to $X$ along the above map for some $n \gg 0$ to a global section 
\[ \tilde{\phi}  \in H^0 (X,    F^e_*\frak{a}_{p^e -1} \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(D),\mathcal O_X (nD_0) ) \]
such that the restriction of $\tilde{\phi}$ to $U$ is equal to $\phi$. In particular, the map $\tilde{\phi}$ sends the canonical section $F^{e}_{*} 1 $ to $1 \in \mathcal O_X (nD_0)$ (defined by the effective divisor $nD_0$). Next, by \autoref{lem:testdivisor} we may choose $e' > 0$ and a map $\psi \in H^0 (X, F_ * ^{e'}  \mathfrak{a} _{p^{e'} - 1} \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om (F_* ^{e'} \mathcal O_X  (nD_0), \mathcal O_X)$ such that $\psi (F_* ^{e'} 1) =  1$. Then, noting that $\tilde{\phi} (-nD_0)$ can be viewed as a map in $   H^0 (X,    F^e_*\frak{a}_{p^e -1} \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(D-np^e D_0),\mathcal O_X  )$, the map 
\[ \psi \star \tilde{\phi} (-nD_0) \in    F^{e+e'} _* (\mathfrak{a}_{p^{e'} -1} ^{[p^e]} \mathfrak{a}_{p^e -1}) \cdot( \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^{e+ e'}_*\mathcal O_X(D),\mathcal O_X) )\]
constructed in \autoref{def:globaloperations} splits $D$ and shows that $D \notin I_{e+e'} ^{\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (\mathcal O_X (D))$ since $\mathfrak{a}_{p^{e' -1}} ^{[p^e]} \mathfrak{a}_{p^e -1} \subset \mathfrak{a}_{p^{e+ e'} - 1} $. This completes the proof of the Proposition. \qedhere
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- dfn-19: body_md -->
Let $R$ be a Noetherian $F$-finite reduced ring. The \emph{full Cartier algebra} $\mathcal{C}(R)$ is defined to be the non-commutative graded algebra
\[ \mathcal{C}(R) := \bigoplus_{e\geq 0} \mathcal{C}_e =  \bigoplus_{e\geq 0} \operatorname{Hom}_R(F^e_*R,R).\]
A \emph{Cartier subalgebra over $R$}, denoted by $\mathcal{D}\subseteq \mathcal{C}(R)$ is a graded subalgebra of $\mathcal{C}$ such that $\mathcal{D}_0 = R$ (under addition and the $\star$-operation). Under the natural grading induced from $\mathcal{C} (R)$, we denote the $e^{\text{th}}$-graded piece of $\mathcal{D}$ by $\mathcal{D}_e \subset \mathcal{C}_e $ which is an $F^{e}_{*} R$-submodule of $\operatorname{Hom}_R(F^e_*R,R)$.
<!-- end dfn-19 -->
<!-- dfn-20: body_md -->
\label{def:Cartiersubalgebras}
    Let $(R, \mathfrak{m}, k)$ be an $F$-finite local domain and $\mathcal{D}$ be a Cartier subalgebra over $R$. Let $I_e ^{\mathcal{D}}$ denote the following ideal of $R$:
\[ I_e^{\mathcal{D}} = \{ f \in R \mid \varphi(F^e_* f) \in \mathfrak{m} \text{ for all } \varphi \in \mathcal{D}_e \}. \]
The pair $(R, \mathcal{D})$ is said to be $F$-regular if for each non-zero element $c \in R$, there exists an $e \gg 0$ such that $c \notin I_e ^\mathcal{D}$.
Next, assume that $\mathcal{D}_e \neq 0$ for all $e \gg 0$. Then, the $F$-signature of the pair $(R, \mathcal{D})$ is defined as
\[ \mathscr{s}(R, \mathcal{D}) := \lim_{e \xrightarrow{\ \ } \infty } \frac{\ell (R/I_e ^\mathcal{D})}{p^{ed}} .\]
Here $\ell$ denotes the length as an $R$-module and $d$ denotes the dimension of $R$.
<!-- end dfn-20 -->
<!-- thm-9: body_md -->
{\cite[Theorems 3.11, 3.18]{BlickleSchwedeTuckerFSigPairs1}} Let $(R, \mathfrak{m}, k)$ be an $F$-finite local domain and $\mathcal{D}$ be a Cartier subalgebra over $R$ such that $\mathcal{D}_e \neq 0$ for all $e \gg 0$. Then, the $F$-signature of $(R, \mathcal{D})$ exists and it is positive if and only if the pair $(R, \mathcal{D})$ is $F$-regular.
<!-- end thm-9 -->
<!-- dfn-21: body_md -->
\label{dfn:lambdagrading}
    Let $\frac{1}{p^\infty} \mbox{$\mathbb{Z}$}$ denote the additive group consisting of fractions of the form $\frac{n}{p^e}$ for some $e \geq 0$ and $n \in \mbox{$\mathbb{Z}$}$. We set $\Lambda : = \mathbb{N} \times \frac{1}{p^\infty} \mbox{$\mathbb{Z}$} $. Then, by the above discussion, the full Cartier algebra of an $\mathbb{N}$-graded ring $S$ is naturally a $\Lambda$-graded non-commutative algebra over $S$, which we denote as
    \[ \mathcal{C}(S) = \bigoplus_{e \geq 0} \bigoplus _{\frac{n}{p^e} \in \frac{1}{p^e}\mbox{$\mathbb{Z}$}}\operatorname{Hom}_S^{\text{gr}}\left(F^e_*S\left[\frac{-n}{p^e}\right], S \right)  .\] We will consider $\Lambda$-graded Cartier subalgebras of $\mathcal{D} \subset \mathcal{C}$ with $\mathcal{D}_0 = S$. Note that for such a subalgebra, each $e^{\text{th}}$-graded component $\mathcal{D}_e$ is a $\frac{1}{p^e} \mbox{$\mathbb{Z}$}$-graded $F^{e}_{*} S$-submodule of  $\operatorname{Hom}_S (F^{e}_{*} S, S)$ and decomposes as
    \[  \mathcal{D}_e = \bigoplus _{\frac{n}{p^e} \in \frac{1}{p^e}\mbox{$\mathbb{Z}$}} \Big ( \mathcal{D}_{e,n} \subset \operatorname{Hom}_S^{\text{gr}}\left(F^e_*S\left[\frac{-n}{p^e}\right], S \right) \Big)  .\]
<!-- end dfn-21 -->
<!-- eg-1: body_md -->
\label{examplesoflambdagraded} There are several natural $\Lambda$-graded Cartier subalgebras that arise over an $\mathbb{N}$-graded ring $S$.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Suppose $S$ is normal and $\Delta$ is an effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor over $Y : = \operatorname{{Spec}}(S)$. Assume that $\Delta$ is \emph{homogeneous}, which means that the prime divisors occuring as components of the support of $\Delta$ are all defined by homogeneous prime ideals in $S$. Then, the Cartier subalgebra over $S$ associated to the pair $(Y, \Delta)$, denoted by $\mathcal{C}(S, \Delta)$ is naturally $\Lambda$-graded as follows:
        \[ \mathcal{C}(S, \Delta)_{e} = \operatorname{Hom}_S (F^{e}_{*} ( S(\lceil (p^e -1) \Delta \rceil) ), S) =  \bigoplus _{\frac{n}{p^e} \in \frac{1}{p^e}\mbox{$\mathbb{Z}$}} \operatorname{Hom}_S^{\text{gr}}\left(F^e_*S (\lceil (p^e -1) \Delta \rceil) \, \left[\frac{-n}{p^e}\right], S \right). \]

        \item Continuing the previous example, suppose moreover that the $\mathbb{N}$-graded ring $S$ is a section ring of a normal projective variety $X$ over $k$ with respect to an ample line bundle $\mathcal{L}$. Let $\Delta$ be an effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor over $X$ and $\tilde{\Delta}$ denote the cone over $\Delta$ with respect to $\mathcal{L}$. Thus, $\tilde{\Delta}$ is a homogeneous $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor on the cone $Y = \operatorname{{Spec}} (S(X, \mathcal{L}))$. Then, the graded pieces of $\mathcal{C}(S, \tilde{\Delta})$ can be understood as (see \autoref{lem.SectionRingVSCoherentSheaf})
        \[ \mathcal{C}(S, \tilde{\Delta})_{e,n} = \operatorname{Hom}_S^{\text{gr}}\left(F^e_*S (\lceil (p^e -1) \tilde{\Delta} \rceil) \, \left[\frac{-n}{p^e}\right], S \right) =  \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}
        (F^{e}_{*} \mathcal O_X (\lceil (p^ e-1) \Delta \rceil), \mathcal{L}^n).  \]

        In particular, by taking $\Delta = 0$, we see that the full Cartier algebra $\mathcal{C} (S)$ naturally consists of graded pieces 
        \[ \mathcal{C} (S) _{e,n} = \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X} (F^{e}_{*} \mathcal O_X, \mathcal{L}^n) = \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X} (F^{e}_{*} \mathcal{L}^{-np^e}, \mathcal O_X) .  \]
        Moreover, under this identification of homogeneous maps, the $\star$-operation on $\mathcal{C}(S)$ applied to homogeneous maps  matches with the global $\star$-operation on maps defined in \autoref{def:globaloperations}.
        
                                                            
        \item Next, suppose $\mathfrak{a}$ is a homogeneous ($\mathbb{N}$-graded) ideal of $S$. Then, $F^{e}_{*} \mathfrak{a}$ is naturally $\frac{1}{p^e} \mathbb{N}$-graded ideal of $F^{e}_{*}  S$. Then, $ F^{e}_{*} \mathfrak{a} \cdot \operatorname{Hom}_S (F^{e}_{*} S, S) $ is a $\frac{1}{p^e} \mbox{$\mathbb{Z}$}$-graded $F^{e}_{*} S$-submodule of  $\operatorname{Hom}_S (F^{e}_{*} S, S)$ which we may compute as follows:
\begin{equation}\label{eqn.decomposition} \begin{split} F^e_* \mathfrak{a} \cdot \operatorname{Hom}_{S}(F^e_*S ,S)& = (F^e_* \mathfrak{a}) \cdot\bigoplus_{\frac{n}{p^e}\in \frac{1}{p^e}\mbox{$\mathbb{Z}$}}\operatorname{Hom}_S \left(F^e_*S, S\right)_{\frac{n}{p^e}} \\ & = \bigoplus _{\frac{m}{p^e} \in \frac{1}{p^e}\mbox{$\mathbb{Z}$}} \quad \sum _{ \ell\in \mathbb {Z}} (F^e_*\frak{a})_{\frac{\ell}{p^e}} \cdot \operatorname{Hom}_{S} (F^e_* S , S) _{\frac{m-\ell}{p^e}}.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Thus, putting this together with \autoref{decompositionofHom}, we see that the graded components of $(F^{e}_{*} \mathfrak{a}) \cdot \operatorname{Hom}_S (F^{e}_{*} S, S)$ are given by
\begin{equation} \label{eqn:decompositioofhomwithideal} \left( (F^{e}_{*} \mathfrak{a}) \cdot \operatorname{Hom}_S (F^{e}_{*} S, S) \right)_{\frac{m}{p^e}}  = \sum _{ \ell\in \mathbb {Z}} (F^e_*\frak{a})_{\frac{\ell}{p^e}} \cdot \operatorname{Hom}_{S} ^{\mathrm{gr}}\left(F^e_* S \left[ \frac{-m+ \ell}{p^e} \right] , S\right).\end{equation}

Thus, given a graded sequence of homogeneous ideals $\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}$ over $S$ (or more generally, an $F$-graded sequence), there is a naturally $\Lambda$-graded Cartier subalgebra $\mathcal{C}(S, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$ defined as follows:
\[ \mathcal{C}(S, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})_{e} = \left( (F^{e}_{*} \mathfrak{a}_{p^e -1}) \cdot \operatorname{Hom}_S (F^{e}_{*} S, S) \right)  \]
where the further decomposition of $\mathcal{C}(S, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})_e = \bigoplus_{\frac{m}{p^e} \in \frac{1}{p^e} \mbox{$\mathbb{Z}$} } \,  \left( (F^{e}_{*} \mathfrak{a}_{p^e -1}) \cdot \operatorname{Hom}_S (F^{e}_{*} S, S) \right)_{\frac{m}{p^e}} $ can be computed using \autoref{eqn:decompositioofhomwithideal}.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end eg-1 -->
<!-- lem-16: body_md -->
\label{lem:simplifiedIegraded}
    With notation as above, for any $e \geq 0$ and $m \geq 0$, we have 
    \[ I_e ^\mathcal{D} (m) = \left\{f\in S_m \mid \varphi(F^e_*f) = 0 \text{ for all } \varphi \in \mathcal{D}_{e,-m}  \right\} \]
<!-- end lem-16 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Note that the $\subseteq$ is straightforward since the right-hand side takes care of the homomorphisms of degree $\frac{-m}{p^e}$. For the converse direction, suppose $f \in S_m$ and $\varphi(F^e_*f) = 0 \text{ for all } \varphi \in \mathcal{D}_{e,-m}$. Then for any homogeneous $\phi \in \mathcal{D}_{e,n}$, we have that $\phi (F^{e}_{*} f) $ is $0$ is $m \not \equiv n \bmod p^e $ or if $ n < -m$. But if $m + n = k p^e $ for some $k > 0$, then $\phi (F^{e}_{*} f)$ has degree $k>0$ and hence already lies in $\mathfrak{m}$. Therefore, we see that $\phi (F^{e}_{*} f) \in \mathfrak{m}$ in any case and therefore for all $\phi \in \mathcal{D}_e$, which shows that $f \in I_e ^\mathcal{D}$.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- dfn-22: body_md -->
\label{def:Cartiersubalgebraassociatedtogradedsequence}
    Let $X$ be a normal projective variety and $\mathcal{L}$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. Let $S=S(X,\mathcal{L})$ denote the section ring of $X$ with respect to $\mathcal{L}$. Then, given a graded sequence of coherent ideal sheaves $\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}$ on $X$ (\autoref{gradedsequencedfn}), we define the associated Cartier subalgebra $\mathcal{D}(S, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}) = \mathcal{D}(X, \mathcal{L}, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$ over $S$ as:
    \[ \mathcal{D}(X, \mathcal{L}, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})_e = \bigoplus _{\frac{m}{p^e} \in \frac{1}{p^e} \mbox{$\mathbb{Z}$}} \Big ( \mathcal{D}_{e,m} :=  H^0 \big( X, F^{e}_{*} \mathfrak{a}_{p^e-1} \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal{L}^{-m},\mathcal O_X)  \big)  \Big).  \]
    It follows from the compatibility of the global $\star$-operation defined in \autoref{def:globaloperations} and the $\star$-operation on $\mathcal{C}(S)$ (see \autoref{examplesoflambdagraded}, (b)) that $\mathcal{D}(S, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$ is indeed a Cartier subalgebra over $S$.
<!-- end dfn-22 -->
<!-- lem-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:relatingIeofgradedsequenceandCartiersubalgebra}
  Let $X$ be a normal projective variety and $\mathcal{L}$ be an ample line bundle on $X$ and $S=S(X,\mathcal{L})$ denote the section ring of $X$ with respect to $\mathcal{L}$. Suppose we have a graded sequence of coherent ideal sheaves $\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}$ on $X$ (\autoref{gradedsequencedfn}) and the associated Cartier subalgebra $\mathcal{D}(S, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}) = \mathcal{D}(X, \mathcal{L}, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$ over $S$ (\autoref{def:Cartiersubalgebraassociatedtogradedsequence}). Then, for all $e \geq 1$ and $m \geq 0$, we have
  \[ I_e ^{\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (\mathcal{L}^m) = I_e ^\mathcal{D} (m).  \]
  Here $I_e ^{\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (\mathcal{L}^m) $ is calculated over $X$ as in \autoref{def:Iebullet} and $I_e ^\mathcal{D}$ is calculated over $S$ as in \autoref{lem:simplifiedIegraded}.
<!-- end lem-17 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Note that $S_m = H^0 (X, \mathcal{L}^m)$ so both  $I_e ^{\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (\mathcal{L}^m)$ and $ I_e ^\mathcal{D} (m)$ are subspaces of $S_m$. By \autoref{lem:simplifiedIegraded}, a homogeneous element $f \in S_m$ is contained in $I_e ^\mathcal{D} (m)$ if and only if $ \varphi (F^{e}_{*} f) = 0 $ for all $\varphi \in \mathcal{D}_{e, -m} = H^0 \big( X, F^{e}_{*} \mathfrak{a}_{p^e-1} \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal{L}^{m},\mathcal O_X)  \big)  \Big) $. But given a map $\varphi \in \operatorname{Hom} _{\mathcal O_X}( F^{e}_{*} \mathcal{L}^m ,  \mathcal O_X)$, the corresponding map $\tilde{\varphi}$ in the Cartier algebra of $S$ is just the cone over the map $\varphi$. Therefore, we have $\varphi (F^{e}_{*} (1_f)) = 0$ if and only $\tilde{\varphi}(f) = 0 $, where we view $ 1_f $ the canonical global section of $\mathcal{L}^m$ defined by $f \in S_m$. This proves the lemma.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
We set $\mathcal{D}$ to be the Cartier subalgebra over $S$ associated to $(X, \mathcal{L}, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$ as in \autoref{def:Cartiersubalgebraassociatedtogradedsequence}.
    
    By the definition of the $F$-signature $\mathscr{s}_X(\mathfrak{a}_\bullet ,L)$ (\autoref{def:fsigofidealsequence}) and \autoref{lem:relatingIeofgradedsequenceandCartiersubalgebra}, we have the equivalent limit 
    \[ \mathscr{s}_X(\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet},L) = \lim_{e \xrightarrow{\ \ }\infty} \frac{1}{p^{e(d+1)}}\sum_{r=0}^\infty \dim \frac{S_r}{I^{\mathcal{D}} _e (r)} \]
    which exists by \cite[Theorem 3.11]{BlickleSchwedeTuckerFSigPairs1}. Note that for any $e \geq 1$, the space $\mathcal{D}_{e,n} = H^0 \big( X, F^{e}_{*} \mathfrak{a}_{p^e-1} \cdot \mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal{L}^{-n},\mathcal O_X)  \big) \neq 0 $ for all $n \gg 0$ by the ampleness of $\mathcal{L}$. $\mathcal{D}_e \neq 0$ for all $ e \geq 0$.

    Next, by \cite[Theorem 3.18]{BlickleSchwedeTuckerFSigPairs1} the positivity of the $F$-signature $\mathscr{s} (S, \mathcal{D})$ is equivalent to the $F$-regularity of the pair $(S, \mathcal{D})$ (see \autoref{def:Cartiersubalgebras}). Therefore, it suffices to check that the $F$-regularity of the pair $(S, \mathcal{D})$ is equivalent to the global $F$-regularity of the pair $(X, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$. Suppose $(S, \mathcal{D})$ is $F$-regular, which by definition means that for each non-zero element $c \in S$, there is some $e \gg 0$ such that $c \notin I_e ^\mathcal{D}$. Applying this to homogeneous elements of $S$ and using \autoref{lem:relatingIeofgradedsequenceandCartiersubalgebra}, we see that for any divisor $D \sim rL$ (for some $r >0$), there exists an $e \gg 0$ such that $D \notin I_e ^{\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (rL)$. By \autoref{prop:testdivisor}, this implies that the pair $(X, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$ is globally $F$-regular. Conversely, suppose $(X, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$ is globally $F$-regular but $(S, \mathcal{D})$ is not $F$-regular. Then, there exists a non-zero element $c \in S$ such that $c \in I_e ^\mathcal{D}$ for all $e \geq 1$. But since the ideals $I_e ^\mathcal{D}$ are homogeneous, this implies that if $c = \sum c_r$ is the homogeneous decomposition of $c$, then each $c_r \in I_e ^\mathcal{D}$ for all $e \geq 1$. But again, using \autoref{lem:relatingIeofgradedsequenceandCartiersubalgebra}, and the global $F$-regularity of $(X, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$, we know that $c_r \notin I_e ^\mathcal{D}$ for $ e \gg 0$. This is a contradiction and shows that $(S, \mathcal{D})$ is $F$-regular. Therefore, by \cite[Theorem 3.18]{BlickleSchwedeTuckerFSigPairs1}, the pair $(X, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$ is globally $F$-regular if and only if the $F$-signature $\mathscr{s}_X (\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}, L)$ is positive. This completes the proof of \autoref{thm:fsigofgradedsequences}.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- dfn-23: body_md -->
Let $X$ be a projective variety and $\mathcal{L}$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. Let $S=S(X,\mathcal{L})$ denote the section ring of $X$ with respect to $\mathcal{L}$. Then, given a graded sequence of coherent ideal sheaves $\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}$ on $X$,
    the \emph{cone over $\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}$} is a graded sequence of ideals $\tilde{\mathfrak{a}}_\bullet$ of $S$ defined by
\[  \tilde{\mathfrak{a}}_n = M(\mathfrak{a}_n, L) := \bigoplus _{r \geq 0} H^0 (X, \mathfrak{a}_n \otimes L^r). \]
We note that since $\mathfrak{a}_m \cdot \mathfrak{a}_n \subset \mathfrak{a}_{m+n} $, the cones $\tilde{\mathfrak{a}}_\bullet$ are automatically a graded sequence since the condition can be checked on homogeneous elements and the image of the map $H^0 (X, \mathfrak{a}_m \otimes L^r) \otimes H^0 (X, \mathfrak{a}_n \otimes L^s) \xrightarrow{\ \ } H^0 (X, L^{r + s} ) $ lies in $H^0 (X, \mathfrak{a}_{m+n} \otimes L^{r+s})$.
<!-- end dfn-23 -->
<!-- dfn-24: body_md -->
\label{def:FsigPair}
Let $X$ be a $d$-dimensional normal variety over $k$. Let $L$ be a big divisor on $X$. The \emph{$F$-signature function of a pair $\mathscr{s}_X(\Delta,L)$} is \[\mathscr{s}_X(\Delta, L) = \lim_{e\xrightarrow{\ \ }\infty}\frac{1}{p^{e(d+1)}}\sum_{m=0}^\infty\dim_k \frac{H^0(mL)}{I_e^\Delta(mL)}\]
<!-- end dfn-24 -->
<!-- thm-10: body_md -->
Let $X$ a normal projective variety and $L$ be a big Cartier divisor. Then,
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The $F$-signature of a pair $s_X(\Delta,  L)$ exists.
    \item (Scaling property) For any $n\in \mathbb{N}$, $s_X(\Delta, nL) = \frac{1}{n} s_X(\Delta,  L)$.
    \item The function $L \mapsto s_X(\Delta, L)$ is locally Lipschitz continuous on the big cone.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end thm-10 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
The key ingredients in establishing the first two properties are \autoref{Pn:twistedFsig} and \autoref{Pn:TransformationRuleFsig}. The arguments adapt directly to $I_e^\Delta$ since the essential part of the proof is comparing the dimensions of the spaces. As a consequence, $\mathscr{s}_X(\Delta,L)$ is locally Lipschitz continuous on the big cone of $X$.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- dfn-25: body_md -->
\label{alphae}
 For each integer $e \geq 1$, we define
\[ m_{e} (X,\Delta , L) : = \max \{ m \geq 0 \, | \, I_{e}^\Delta (mL)  = 0 \}, \]
where $I_e^\Delta(L)$ is the subspace defined as above. We also define
\[ \alpha_{e}(X,\Delta, L) := \frac{m_e (X,\Delta, L)}{p^e} .\] The \emph{$\alpha_F$-invariant of pairs} is $\alpha(X,\Delta,L)= \lim_{e\xrightarrow{\ \ }\infty} \alpha_e(X,\Delta,L)$.
<!-- end dfn-25 -->
<!-- pn-10: body_md -->
\label{Pn:AlphaInvPairsPropositions}
Let $X$ be a normal projective variety and $L$ be an integral big divisor on $X$. Let $\Delta$ be an effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor on $X$. Then,
\begin{enumerate}
\item the $\alpha_F$-invariant $\alpha(X,\Delta,L)$ exists.
\item for any $n\in \mathbb{N}$, $\alpha_F(X,\Delta, nL) = \frac{1}{n}\alpha_F(X,\Delta, L)$.

\end{enumerate}
<!-- end pn-10 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
The first part is similar to  \autoref{lem:AlphaInvExists} together with \cite[Lemma 4.5]{PandeFrobeniusVersionTiansAlphaInvariant} to deal with the difference of rounding. The second follows by an analogous argument using \autoref{Prop:transformationforalpha}, since the proof relies on the index $m_e$ that makes $I_e^\Delta$ trivial and the linear spaces of big divisors $|mL|$ for $m\gg0$.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- pn-11: body_md -->
Let $X$ be a normal projective variety and $L$ be a big $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier divisor on $X$. Let $\Delta$ be an effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor on $X$. Then, \begin{enumerate}
\item for any effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $E$, $\alpha_F(X, \Delta, L) \geq \alpha_F(X, \Delta, L+E)$.
\item the alpha invariant is locally Lipschitz continuous on the big cone.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end pn-11 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
For the first part, let $n$ and $m$ be the Cartier indices of $L$ and $E$, respectively, and set $L' = mnL$ and $E' = mnE$. Since $I_e^\Delta(L') \subseteq I_e^\Delta(L' + E')$, it follows that $m_e(X, \Delta, L') \geq m_e(X, \Delta, L' + E')$. Together with \autoref{Pn:AlphaInvPairsPropositions} and the definition of $\alpha_F$, the desired inequality follows. For the second part, recall that the continuity of the non-pair version of $\alpha_F$ relies on \autoref{Prop:addingeffective} and \autoref{lem:upperboundonalpha}. The first part above provides the paired analogue of \autoref{Prop:addingeffective}. Moreover, by definition, we have $\alpha_F(X, \Delta, L) \leq \alpha_F(X, L)$, so $\alpha_F(X, \Delta, L)$ satisfies the same upper bound as in \autoref{lem:upperboundonalpha}. Therefore, by running the same argument as in \autoref{Prop:alphacontinuity}, we obtain the continuity of the alpha invariant of the pair.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- dfn-26: body_md -->
\label{def:FsigTriple}
Let $X$ be a $d$-dimensional normal projective variety. Let $(X, \Delta, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$ be a triple as above and $L$ be a big divisor on $X$. We define the \emph{F-signature function of the triple}, denoted $s_X(\Delta, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}, L)$, as:
\[
s_X(\Delta, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}, L) = \lim_{e \xrightarrow{\ \ } \infty} \frac{1}{p^{e(d+1)}} \sum_{m=0}^{\infty} \dim_k \frac{H^0(mL)}{I_e^{\Delta, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}}(mL)}.
\]
<!-- end dfn-26 -->
<!-- thm-11: body_md -->
Let $X$ a normal projective variety and $L$ be a big Cartier divisor. Let $\frak{a}_\bullet$ be a graded sequence of ideal sheaves on $X$. Then,
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The $F$-signature of triple $s_X(\Delta, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}, L)$ exists.
    \item (Scaling property) For any $n\in \mathbb{N}$, $s_X(\Delta, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}, nL) = \frac{1}{n} s_X(\Delta, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}, L)$.
    \item The function $L \mapsto s_X(\Delta, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}, L)$ is locally Lipschitz continuous on the big cone.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end thm-11 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
The proof is identical to the pair version when $\frak{a}_\bullet$ is trivial. Hence, we omit the proof.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- dfn-27: body_md -->
For a triple $(X, \Delta, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$ and a big divisor $L$, we define:
\[ m_e(X, \Delta, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}, L) := \max \{ m \ge 0 \mid I_e^{\Delta, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}}(mL) = 0 \}. \]
The \emph{$\alpha_F$-invariant of the triple} is defined as $\alpha_F(X, \Delta, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}, L) := \lim_{e \xrightarrow{\ \ } \infty} \frac{m_e(X, \Delta, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}, L)}{p^e}$.
<!-- end dfn-27 -->
<!-- pn-12: body_md -->
\label{Pn:AlphaInvPairsPropositions}
Let $(X,\Delta,\frak{a}_\bullet) $ be a triple and $L$ be an integral big divisor on $X$. Then,
\begin{enumerate}
\item the $\alpha_F$-invariant $\alpha(X,\Delta,\frak{a}_\bullet,L)$ exists.
\item for any $n\in \mathbb{N}$, $\alpha_F(X,\Delta,\frak{a}_\bullet, nL) = \frac{1}{n}\alpha_F(X,\Delta,\frak{a}_\bullet, L)$.

\end{enumerate}
<!-- end pn-12 -->
<!-- pn-13: body_md -->
Let $(X,\Delta, \frak{a}_\bullet)$ be a triple and $L$ be a big $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier divisor on $X$. Then, \begin{enumerate}
\item for any effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $E$, $\alpha_F(X,\Delta,\frak{a}_\bullet, L) \geq \alpha_F(X,\Delta,\frak{a}_\bullet, L+E)$.
\item the alpha invariant is locally Lipschitz continuous on the big cone.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end pn-13 -->
<!-- thm-12: body_md -->
\label{Thm:transformationRuleProperBirational}
    Let $X$ be a globally $F$-regular projective variety and $L$ be a big and semi-ample divisor over $X$. Suppose $\pi: X \xrightarrow{\ \ } Y$ is the birational contraction defined by $|mL|$ for some $ m \gg 0$ sufficiently divisible and $L_0$ denote the ample divisor on $Y$ such that $\pi ^* L_0 \sim L$. Then, we have
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Suppose $K_Y $ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier and $K_{X|Y} = K_X - \pi^* K_Y \leq 0$. Then,  $\mathscr{s}_X (L) = \mathscr{s}_Y (L_0) $.

        \item Suppose $K_Y $ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier and we have $K_{X|Y} = E \geq 0$ for some effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $E$. Then, we have a natural graded sequence of ideal sheaves over $Y$ defined by
        \[ \mathfrak{a}_m := \pi_* \mathcal O_X (\lfloor -mE \rfloor ).  \]
        Moreover, we have the following transformation rule for the $F$-signature:
        \[ \mathscr{s}_X (L) = \mathscr{s}_Y (\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}, L_0). \]
        
        \item For any effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $\Delta_X $ such that $(X, \Delta_X)$ is globally $F$-regular and $-K_X - \Delta_X  \sim _\mathbb{Q} L$, we have:
        \begin{itemize}
            \item setting $\Delta_Y = \pi_* \Delta_X $, the pair $(Y, \Delta_Y)$ is globally $F$-regular.

            \item the divisor $- K_Y - \Delta_Y$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier and $ - K_Y - \Delta_Y \sim _\mathbb{Q} L_0 $.

            \item We have 
            \[ \mathscr{s}_X (\Delta_X, L) = \mathscr{s}_Y (\Delta_Y, L_0).\]
        \end{itemize}
        
    \end{enumerate}
Here $\mathscr{s}_Y(\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet},L_0)$ is the $F$-signature defined in \autoref{def:fsigofidealsequence}, while the $F$-signatures
of divisor pairs are defined in \autoref{def:FsigPair}.
<!-- end thm-12 -->
<!-- eg-2: body_md -->
We provide an example of a smooth blow-up for \autoref{Thm:transformationRuleProperBirational}. In fact, it provides an asymptotic generalization of \cite[Proposition 2.1]{LakshmibaiFrobSplittingsandBlowups}. Let $X$ be a smooth globally $F$-regular projective variety and let $Z\subset X$ be a smooth subvariety of codimension $d\geq 2$. 
Consider the blow-up $\pi:Y = \mathrm{Bl}_Z(X) \xrightarrow{\ \ } X $ along $Z$. Let $E$ be the exceptional divisor. Then, the relative canonical $K_{Y|X} = (d-1)E$ is effective. Let $\frak{a}_m = \pi_*\mathcal O_Y(\lfloor -m(d-1)E\rfloor)$. Then, for any ample divisor $L$ on $X$, we have $\mathscr{s}_Y(\pi^*L) = \mathscr{s}_X(\frak{a}_\bullet, L)$ by \autoref{Thm:transformationRuleProperBirational}.
<!-- end eg-2 -->
<!-- lem-18: body_md -->
\label{lem:multiplicationandtracemap}
    Let $X$ be a normal projective variety, $\Delta$ an effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor and $\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet} $ a graded sequence of ideal sheaves over $X$ (\autoref{gradedsequencedfn}). Then, for any $e \geq 1$ and any Weil-divisor $D $, let $\mathcal{F}_{e, \Delta, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (D)$ denote the sheaf $ \mathfrak{a}_{p^e  -1 } \cdot (\mathcal O_X( (1-p^e)K_X -  \lceil (p^e - 1) \Delta \rceil )  -D )$ over $X$. Then,  
    the subspace $I_e ^{\Delta, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (D)$ can be described as follows:
    \[ I_e ^{\Delta, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (D) = \{ f \in H^0 (\mathcal O_X (D)) \, | \, \text{Tr} ^e _\Delta (F^{e}_{*} (fg)) = 0 \text{ for all } g \in H^0 (\mathcal{F}_{e, \Delta, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (D)) \}. \]
<!-- end lem-18 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
Note that by the duality for the Frobenius map, we have an isomorphism
\[ \mathscr{H}om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(\lceil (p^e-1)\Delta \rceil +D), \mathcal O_X) \cong F^{e}_{*} (\mathcal O_X( (1-p^e)K_X -  \lceil (p^e - 1) \Delta \rceil )  -D ).   \]
Via this isomorphism, we may identify any section $g \in H^0 (\mathcal{F}_{e,\Delta, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (D)$ with a section of $    H^0(F^{e}_{*}\frak{a}_{p^e-1} \cdot\mathscr{H}\kern -.3pt om_{\mathcal O_X}(F^e_*\mathcal O_X(\lceil (p^e-1)\Delta \rceil + D),\mathcal O_X))$
which is in turn a subspace of 
\[ H^0 (X, F^{e}_{*} (\mathcal O_X( (1-p^e)K_X -  \lceil (p^e - 1) \Delta \rceil )  -D ) ).\] Now the lemma follows from
\cite[Lemma 2.17]{PandeFrobeniusVersionTiansAlphaInvariant}
and the definition of $I_e^{\Delta,\mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}}(D)$ in
\autoref{subsec:triples}.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- lem-19: body_md -->
\label{lem.PushDownComparison}
    With notation as above, for each $e \geq 1$ such that $(1-p^e) K_X$ is Cartier, we have the following commutative diagram:
    \[
\xymatrix{
H^0(F^{e}_{*} \mathcal O_Y((1-p^e)K_Y)) \ar[d]^{\pi_*}  \ar[r]^<<<<{\operatorname{Tr} ^e} & H^0 (Y, \mathcal O_Y) = k\ar[d]^{\pi_*}_\sim \\
 H^0(F^e_*\mathcal O_X((1-p^e)K_X))\ar[r]\ar[r]^<<<<{\operatorname{Tr} ^e}& H^0 (X, \mathcal O_X) = k 
}
\]
<!-- end lem-19 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
This follows from the definition of the trace-map, which, under duality for the Frobenius map, is identified with the evaluation at $F^{e}_{*} 1$ map
\[  \mathscr{H}om _{\mathcal O_X} (F^{e}_{*} \mathcal O_X, \mathcal O_X) \xrightarrow{\ \ } \mathcal O_X  .\]
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- thm-13: body_md -->
\label{thm.GlobalFregularityProperBirational}
Let $\pi: X \xrightarrow{\ \ } Y$ be a proper birational map between normal, projective varieties over $k$. Suppose we have an effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $\Delta_Y$ on $Y$ such that $K_Y + \Delta_Y$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier. Write $K_ X + \Delta_X = \pi^* (K_Y + \Delta_Y) + E$, where $\Delta_X$ is the strict transform of $\Delta_Y$ along $Y$ and $E$ denotes some $\pi$-exceptional $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor over $X$. Let $\mathfrak{a}_\bullet$ denote the graded sequence of ideal sheaves defined by
\[ \mathfrak{a}_m = \pi_* \mathcal O_X(\lfloor -mE \rfloor ) \]
for any $m \geq 1$.
Then, we have
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $(X, \Delta_X)$ is globally $F$-regular if and only if the triple $(Y, \Delta_Y, \mathfrak{a}_\bullet)$ is globally $F$-regular.
    \item For any ample divisor $L_0$ on $Y$, we have the equality of $F$-signatures
    \[ \mathscr{s}_X( \Delta_X, \pi^* L_0) = \mathscr{s}_Y( \Delta_Y, \mathfrak{a}_\bullet ,L_0). \]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end thm-13 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
Both parts rely on the following key observation: for any $e \geq 1$ and any Cartier divisor $D$, we have an equality
\begin{equation} \label{eqn:Ieequality} I_e ^{\Delta_X} (\pi^* D) = \pi^* (I_e ^{\Delta_Y, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (D) ).   \end{equation}
 Let $\mathcal{F}_{e, \Delta_Y} (Y, D)$ denote the sheaf $ \mathfrak{a}_{p^e  -1 } \cdot (\mathcal O_Y( (1-p^e)K_Y -  \lceil (p^e - 1) \Delta_X \rceil )  -D )$ on $Y$ and $\mathcal{D}_{e, \Delta_X} ( X,D)$ the divisor $(1-p^e)K_X - \lceil (p^e  -1 ) \Delta_X \rceil - \pi^* D)$ on $X$. Following \autoref{lem.PushDownComparison}, let us consider the following commutative diagram
\[ \begin{tikzcd}
H^0(F^{e}_{*} \mathcal O_X(\pi^*D)) \ar[d, "\pi_*"] & [-3em] \times & [-3em] H^0(F^{e}_{*} \mathcal O_X(\mathcal{D}_{e, \Delta_X} (X, D)) ) \ar[d, "\pi_*"] \ar[r,"F^{e}_{*} \cdot"] & [-1em] H^0 (F^{e}_{*} \mathcal O_X( \mathcal{D}_{e, \Delta_X} (X,0) )) \ar[d, "\pi_*"]    \ar[r, "\operatorname{Tr}^e _{\Delta_X}"] & [1em] k \ar[d, " \cong "] \\
H^0(F^{e}_{*} \mathcal O_Y(D))  &  \times &  H^0 ( F^{e}_{*} \mathcal{F}_{e, \Delta} (Y, D) )   \ar[r, "F^{e}_{*} \cdot"] &  H^0 (F^{e}_{*} \mathcal O_X( F^{e}_{*} \mathcal{F}_{e, \Delta_Y} (Y, 0) ) ) \ar[r, "\operatorname{Tr}^e _{\Delta_Y}"] & k 
\end{tikzcd} \]
where the horizontal maps $F^{e}_{*} \cdot $ are induced by multiplication of sections (before applying $F^{e}_{*}$) as in \autoref{lem:multiplicationandtracemap}. Now, since we have $(1-p^e)K_X - \lceil (p^e  -1 ) \Delta_X \rceil  = \pi^* \big ( (1-p^e)K_Y - \lceil (p^e  -1 ) \Delta_Y \rceil  \big ) -\lfloor (1-p^e)E \rfloor $, we see that
\[
\begin{aligned}
\pi_* H^0(X, \mathcal O_X(\mathcal{D}_{e, \Delta_X} (X, D))) &= \pi_* H^0(X, \pi^* \big ( (1-p^e)K_Y - \lceil (p^e  -1 ) \Delta_Y \rceil  \big ) -\lfloor (1-p^e)E \rfloor )\\
  &= H^0(Y , \mathcal{F}_{e, \Delta_Y} (Y, D) ) \text{\hskip 20pt $(\ast)$}
  \end{aligned} \]
by the projection formula. Therefore, all the vertical maps in the above diagram are isomorphisms.
By \autoref{lem:multiplicationandtracemap}, a section $f \in H^0 (Y, \mathcal O_Y (D))  $ is contained in $I_e ^{\Delta_Y, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (D) $ if and only if for all $ g \in H^0 (\mathcal{F}_{e, \Delta_Y} (Y,D) ) $, we have $\text{Tr}^e _{\Delta_Y} (F^{e}_{*} (fg)) = 0 $. Similarly, $\pi^* (f) \in I_e ^{\Delta_X} (\pi^* D) $ if and only if for all $g \in H^0 (X, \mathcal O_X (\mathcal O_X (\mathcal{D}_{e, \Delta_X} (X,D)) ) )$, we have $\text{Tr} ^e _{\Delta_X} (F^{e}_{*} (fg))  = 0$. Therefore, the equality in \autoref{eqn:Ieequality} follows from the commutativity of the above diagram and the fact that the vertical maps are isomorphisms.



For (a), suppose first that $(X, \Delta_X)$ is globally $F$-regular and we wish to show that $(Y, \Delta_Y, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$ is globally $F$-regular. Let $D$ be an effective Cartier divisor on $Y$. Since $(X, \Delta_X)$ is globally $F$-regular, we know that for all $e \gg 0$, the global section $1 = \pi ^* 1 \in H^ 0 (X, \mathcal O_X (\pi^* (D)))$ is not contained in $I_e ^{\Delta_X} (\pi^* (D))$. Therefore, by \autoref{eqn:Ieequality}, $1 \notin I_e ^{\Delta_Y, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}}$. Since $D$ was arbitrary, we conclude that $(Y, \Delta_Y, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$ is globally $F$-regular.

Conversely, suppose $(Y, \Delta_Y, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$ is globally $F$-regular and we need to show that so is $(X, \Delta_X)$. Fix a very ample divisor $L$ on $X$. By \autoref{prop:testdivisor}, it suffices to show that for any effective divisor $D \sim L$ on $X$, we have $D \notin I_e ^{\Delta_X} (L)$ for $ e \gg 0$. We may choose a sufficiently ample effective divisor $H$ on $Y$ such that $\pi^* H \geq D$. Then, since $(Y, \Delta_Y, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet})$ is globally $F$-regular, we know that for all $e \gg 0$, we have $1 \notin I_e ^{\Delta_Y, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (H)$. By \autoref{eqn:Ieequality} again, we see that $1 \notin I_e ^{\Delta_X} (\pi^* H)$ for all $e \gg 0$. Since $\pi^* H \geq D$, we see that $D \notin I_e ^{\Delta_X} (L)$ as required.


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             

 
For (b), we see immediately from \autoref{eqn:Ieequality} that for all $m \geq 0$ and all $e >0$, we have
\[ \dim_k H^0 (\mathcal O_X (m\pi^*L_0))/ I_e ^{\Delta_X} (m\pi^*L_0) = \dim_k H^0 (\mathcal O_Y (mL_0))/ I_e ^{\Delta_Y, \mathfrak{a}_{\bullet}} (mL_0). \]
Then the claim follows from \autoref{def:FsigPair}
and \autoref{def:FsigTriple}.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
\label{Cor:numericallytrivial}
    Let $X$ be a globally $F$-regular projective variety $\pi:X\xrightarrow{\ \ } Y$ be a projective birational map where $Y$ is normal. Suppose that there is a $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $\Delta_X\geq 0 $ such that $-K_X - \Delta_X \sim _{\mathbb{Q}, \pi} 0  $ and $(X,\Delta_X)$ is globally $F$-regular. Set $\Delta_Y := \pi_*\Delta_X$. Then,\begin{itemize}
\item $K_Y+\Delta_Y$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier and $K_X + \Delta_X = \pi^*(K_Y+\Delta_Y)$.

\item $(Y, \Delta_Y)$ is globally $F$-regular.

\item Moreover, for any ample divisor $L$ on $Y$, we have $\mathscr{s} (X,  \Delta_X; \pi^*L) = \mathscr{s} (Y, \Delta_Y; L)$
\end{itemize}
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
If the first claim holds, then we automatically have that $(Y,\Delta_Y)$ is globally $F$-regular by \cite{SchwedeSmithLogFanoVsGloballyFRegular}. Moreover, by \autoref{thm.GlobalFregularityProperBirational}, the equality of the $F$-signatures follows as well since the corresponding sequence of ideals sheaves will be trivial.

Hence, it suffices to show $K_Y+\Delta_Y$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier and its pullback equals $K_X + \Delta_X$. Take $m>0$ such that $mK_X + m\Delta_X \sim \pi^*M$ where $M$ is a Cartier divisor on $Y$. Then, $\pi_*(mK_X + m\Delta_X)\sim M$ by the projection formula. Here, by construction, $\pi_*(K_X + \Delta_X) = K_Y+\Delta_Y$.  Hence, $K_Y+\Delta_Y$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier. Now, let $F = K_X + \Delta_X - \pi^*(K_Y+\Delta_Y)$ be a divisor supported on the exceptional locus. Since $K_X + \Delta_X$ is assumed to be $\mathbb{Q}$-linearly $\pi$-trivial, $F$ is a $\pi$-numerically trivial effective divisor. By the negativity lemma (which holds in positive characteristics by \cite[Section 2.3]{Birkar16}), we have $F = 0$. Thus, the claim follows.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Part (b) is a special case of \autoref{thm.GlobalFregularityProperBirational}(b) by setting $\Delta_X = \Delta_Y = 0$. Part (a) also follows from
\autoref{thm.GlobalFregularityProperBirational}(b),
with $\Delta_X=\Delta_Y=0$, since $K_{X|Y}\leq 0$
implies that the associated graded sequence
\[
\mathfrak{a}_m=\pi_*\mathcal O_X(\lfloor-mK_{X|Y}\rfloor)=\mathcal O_Y
\]
is trivial. Part (c) is a special case of \autoref{Cor:numericallytrivial} since $K_X + \Delta_X \sim_\mathbb{Q} - \pi^* L $ is $\mathbb{Q}$-linearly $\pi$-trivial. Thus, we have proved \autoref{Thm:transformationRuleProperBirational}.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- not-2: body_md -->
\label{notation:spreadingout}
    For a normal projective variety $X$ over $\mathbb{C}$, we may consider its positive characteristic models $X_p$ for $p \gg 0$ by picking a suitable finitely generated $\mathbb{Z}$-algebra and a model $X_A$ of $X$ over $A$. Consider a closed point $s\in \operatorname{{Spec}} A$ and let $p $ be the characteristic of $k(s)$. A characteristic $p$ model of $X$ is any closed fiber $X_s$ of $X_A \xrightarrow{\ \ } \operatorname{{Spec}} (A)$. Let $L$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. We will denote $L_s$ be the corresponding line bundle on $X_s$ on the characteristic $p$ models for $p \gg 0$.
<!-- end not-2 -->
<!-- conjecture-1: body_md -->
{\cite{carvajal-rojas_fundamental_2016}} \label{conj:CRST}
With the above set up, assume that $X$ is of globally $F$-regular type. Then, after possibly replacing $A$ by a localization, there is a constant $C>0$ (not depending on $p$) such that for all $p \gg 0$ and any characteristic $p$ model $(X_s, L_s)$ of $(X,L)$, we have
\[ \mathscr{s} (X_s, L_s) \geq C . \]
<!-- end conjecture-1 -->
<!-- thm-14: body_md -->
\label{thm:LowerBoundsSpreadout}
    Let $X$ be a projective variety of globally $F$-regular type over $\mathbb{C}$. Suppose we have an ample divisor $L$ and a constant $C:= C(L)$ such that for all $p \gg 0$, we have the lower bound $ \mathscr{s} (X_s, L_s) \geq C $ for all $p \gg 0$. Then, for any ample divisor $L'$ on $X$, after possibly enlarging $A$, there exists a constant $C' := C' (L')$ such that $\mathscr{s} (X_s, L'_s) \geq C'$ for all closed points $s \in \operatorname{{Spec}} (A)$ of characteristic $p$ and all $p \gg 0$.
<!-- end thm-14 -->
<!-- lem-20: body_md -->
\label{lem:equivalentFsigandalpha}  \cite[Lemma 3.7]{LiuPandepositivitylimitfsignature}
Let $X$ be a globally $F$-regular type over $\mathbb{C}$ and $L$ be an ample divisor on $X$. Then keeping \autoref{notation:spreadingout}, the following are equivalent after possibly replacing $A$ by a localization:

\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists a constant $C>0$ independent of $p$ such that $s(X_s, L_s) >C$ for all closed points $s \in \operatorname{{Spec}} (A)$ of characteristic $p$.

\item there exists a constant $D>0$ independent of $p$ such that $\alpha_F(X_s, L_s) >D$ for all closed points $s \in \operatorname{{Spec}} (A)$ of characteristic $p$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-20 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
First, working over $\mathbb{C}$, we pick a constant $\lambda \in \mathbb{\mathbb{Q}}_{>0}$ such that the line joining $\lambda L$ and  $ L'$ in the ample cone is effective (even ample). In other words, we write
    $\lambda L = L' + E$ for some effective Cartier divisor $E $.
    
  

    After possibly enlarging $A$, consider models $X_A, L_A, L'_A, E_A$ of $X, L, L', E$ respectively. Then we may assume that for all closed points $s \in \operatorname{{Spec}} (A)$, we have $E_s$ is an effective Cartier divisor and $\lambda L_s  = L'_s + E_s$.
    
Now, by \autoref{lem:equivalentFsigandalpha}, we know that there is a constant $D>0$ (not depending on $p$) such that for all closed points $s \in \operatorname{{Spec}} (A)$ with characteristic $p \gg 0$, we have $\alpha_{F} (X_s, L_s) \geq D$. Then, using parts (c) and (d) of \autoref{thm:alphaonbigcone}
we have
\[ \alpha_{F} (L' _s) \geq \alpha_{F}(\lambda L_s ) \geq \frac{D}{\lambda} \]
for all closed points $s \in \operatorname{{Spec}} (A)$ with characteristic $p \gg 0$. Finally, since $\lambda$ is independent of $p$, using \autoref{lem:equivalentFsigandalpha} again, there exists a constant $C >0$ such that $\mathscr{s}(X_s, L'_s) \geq C$ for all closed points $s \in \operatorname{{Spec}} (A)$ of characteristic $p \gg 0$. This completes the proof of \autoref{thm:LowerBoundsSpreadout}.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- eg-3: body_md -->
We may apply \autoref{thm:LowerBoundsSpreadout} to the case of cubic surfaces. For any cubic surface $X$ over $\mathbb{C}$ with Du val singularities, the anti-canonical section ring $S(X, -K_X)$ defines a non-weakly exceptional three-dimensional KLT singularity, and hence by \cite{LiuPandepositivitylimitfsignature}, \autoref{conj:CRST} holds for $S(X, -K_X)$. Then, \autoref{thm:LowerBoundsSpreadout} allows us to conclude that \autoref{conj:CRST} holds for every section ring $S(X, L)$ of the cubic surface $X$ with respect to any ample divisor $L$ over $X$. We do not know any other direct method to \autoref{conj:CRST} for all section rings of cubic surfaces, since they may not support a non-weakly exceptional KLT singularity on the cone.
<!-- end eg-3 -->
